USS Abraham Lincoln is set to dock in Thailand next week, giving sailors a chance for “rest and recreation” after reports of declining conditions and mental health issues onboard the ship.

The aircraft carrier departed the Middle East on Saturday and has gone without a port visit for more than 200 days, setting a record for consecutive days spent at sea. Standard naval deployments usually last between six and nine months, though active conflicts can lead to extensions.

Carrying roughly 5,000 sailors and Marines, the warship will arrive in Thailand next week for "rest and recreation after their long sea journey,” a Thai official said Tuesday.

Thailand's Navy confirmed that a U.S. Navy carrier strike group would make a brief stop in eastern Thailand for rest and recuperation, with no military exercises taking place. Citing security concerns, it did not identify the three vessels or supply a date for the visit.

open image in gallery The Lincoln left its home port of San Diego in November and was ​later redirected ​to the Middle ⁠East to support U.S. military operations in the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran ( K.C. Alfred/The San Diego Union- )

"The stop is a routine port visit intended to allow personnel to rest and recuperate ... as well as to receive logistical support," a spokesperson for the Thai Navy said in a statement.

After leaving its home port of San Diego in November, the Lincoln was redirected to the Middle East to support U.S. military operations in the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran.

Worries for troops on the ship grew earlier this month when two defense publications, Navy Times and Stars and Stripes, reported suicide attempts and falling morale on the carrier. U.S. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth brushed off the concerns, stating that the reports "completely misrepresented" conditions on board.

Thailand serves as the United States' sole treaty partner in mainland Southeast Asia, remaining a treaty ally since 1954 and a major non-NATO ally since 2003. Both nations' militaries preserve close relations.

Father of USS Lincoln sailor arrested by Border Patrol

The ship made headlines again over the weekend after the immigrant father of a U.S. sailor on board the USS Abraham Lincoln was taken into federal immigration custody ‌and remains in detention.

U.S. ⁠Border Patrol arrested Luis Manuel Aviles Roa, originally from Nicaragua, after stopping a car in Key West, Florida, a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security said Sunday.

open image in gallery Joshua Aviles, a U.S. sailor deployed in the Middle East during the Iran war, stands next to his immigrant father who was taken into federal immigration detention ( Reuters )

"I've been deployed ⁠for over nine months, out at ​sea ⁠in the Middle East aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, fighting for a country that has given me everything," Joshua Aviles, the ⁠son of the detained immigrant, wrote on Facebook.

"I just got a call ​that ⁠my dad was taken ‌by ICE," he said Saturday, adding that his father had his driver's license, Social Security card and work permit.

"We have done everything through immigration ‌to get his green card approved, and we ‌are just waiting. This is heartbreaking for me. I don't know how I can mentally continue working 12+ hour days knowing that my dad is somewhere, possibly being treated like ⁠a criminal," Joshua Aviles wrote.

DHS said Luis Manuel Aviles Roa entered the U.S. illegally and would remain in Immigration and Customs Enforcement detention pending removal proceedings.

If you are experiencing feelings of distress, or are struggling to cope, you can speak to the Samaritans, in confidence, on 116 123 (UK and ROI) or visit the Samaritans website to find details of your nearest branch.

If you are based in the USA, and you or someone you know needs mental health assistance right now, call or text 988, or visit 988lifeline.org to access online chat from the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This is a free, confidential crisis hotline that is available to everyone 24 hours a day, seven days a week. If you are in another country, you can go to www.befrienders.org to find a helpline near you

A British green technology company is seeking to help create Africa's "energy grid of the future" to reduce reliance on fossil fuels after signing an agreement to invest up to $75 million (£55m) in Nigeria by 2030.

The company, MOPO – based in Sheffield – creates hubs to charge and rent solar-powered batteries in communities where reliable access to electricity is difficult. The batteries themselves are designed, tested and managed from the city. The company 1.6 million battery rentals a month in Nigeria, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Sierra Leone, Liberia, Chad, and Uganda, up from 150,000 in 2023. In total, MOPO has completed 45 million battery rentals across the continent.

The fresh funds include backing from Octopus Energy and other investors including Norfund – the Norwegian government's development investment fund – and the World Bank’s International Finance Corporation (IFC). They will support the development of MOPOGrid, which will expand the services of MOPO’s hubs to help provide cabled electricity, on top of the battery rentals. Recently, MOPO signed an agreement with Nigeria's Rural Electrification Agency to fast-track the pilot phase of this network across the country.

Balogun Adedayo Michael, a tailor based in Epe – just outside Lagos – is clear about the importance of reliable access to electricity, having been without access to the grid for two years. We’ve been suffering because without electricity, we can’t use the industrial machine to sew properly.” Mr Michael said.

He had been using a petrol-powered generator, but fuel prices kept increasing and the generator itself kept breaking down. During local celebrations, when Mr Michael had a high demand from his customers, he said he had to make a change and rented a MOPO battery for power. “I didn’t disappoint them.” he said. In future, instead of renting batteries, Mr Michael could be linked up to their nearest MOPO hub with overhead cables that would make his electrical supply even more reliable.

The funding for MOPO comes as countries deal with significant aid cuts to help fund an increase in UK defence funding, with spending set to fall by around 42 per cent – or £6.5 billion – from a record high in 2023 to a historic low in 2027/28, according to a report by the Independent Commission for Aid Impact (ICAI). Nine African countries are set to see their UK bilateral aid cut by more than 80 per cent by 2028/29, as bilateral spending falls from £1.6bn to under £700m. Nigeria will see its aid cut by around 50 per cent, to £68m.

open image in gallery Balogun Adedayo Michael, a tailor based in Epe, just outside Lagos ( Raychel Kenny/MOPO )

MOPO’s chief operating officer, Luke Burras, said of their expansion: “Being headquartered in Sheffield, we’re very aware of the industrial history. Now we’re innovating with two technologies which are at the heart of another industrial revolution, battery and solar... To us, the grid of the future is super flexible and powered by sunshine.”

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) has said it is pivoting towards investor partnerships with nations, with support of MOPO a reflection of that. Since 2020 the UK has provided MOPO with nearly £4m in investments, while the UK’s development finance institution, British International Investment (BII), has invested £5.2m in MOPO’s expansion in the DRC.

The foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, said of MOPO: “By backing companies like MOPO to grow internationally, they can expand their vital work bringing reliable clean energy to some of the most vulnerable communities across Africa.

“The global clean energy transition is one of the biggest economic opportunities of our time and the UK is at the forefront of it,” he added.

Andy Burnham’s ambitions to build tens of thousands of new council houses is under threat because of a labour shortage caused by Brexit, industry leaders have warned.

A lack of skilled workers and the impact of millions not being able to work here since Brexit means more than 200,000 EU workers have left the industry since 2019, according to Checkatrade's UK Trade Skills Index.

It comes as the latest Office for National Statistics figures show there were 31,000 vacancies in the construction sector between May and July this year – a rise of 2.3 per cent from the same period last year. That figure has, however, fallen since a record 51,000 vacancies in 2022 after Covid.

The crisis is worsened by an aging workforce, with just one in five workers aged under 30 – compared to 35 per cent aged over 50, with many are expected to retire over the next decade, according to the skills index.

Andy Burnham hopes to build tens of thousands of council houses ( PA )

It estimates around 1 million additional workers will be needed to replace those leaving and to meet the additional demand for housebuilding over the next decade. Around 206,000 of those are needed by 2030 from 2025, an upscale of 1.6 per cent in workforce, to meet forecasted demand.

Clive Dickin, chief executive of the National Access and Scaffolding Confederation (NASC), warned that there is a forecast shortage of 40,000 scaffolders alone over the next five years and said that the reflected wider problems in skilled labour since the UK left the EU.

Mr Dickin described the combination of Brexit and Covid as “a perfect storm” which saw thousands of skilled labourers, including scaffolders, leave the country when changes to immigration rules after leaving the EU were brought in, meaning most did not return.

The warning comes as the prime minister unveiled £10bn of funding to build 70,000 new council homes across England feeding into a wider Labour Party target of 1.5 million new homes built by the next election in 2029.

The announcement came just hours after Mr Burnham confirmed that he would stick to Keir Starmer’s controversial “red lines” on Brexit, which rules out rejoining the EU, single market or Customs Union and a return to free movement of people.

Mr Dickin told The Independent: “At the moment we are looking at about a 40,000 vacancy rate. We've got about 130,000 scaffolders, and 40,000 more over the next five years is what we're estimating to meet the demands of the varying house building targets, net zero, cladding initiatives. You know, all of these subject areas are putting greater demands.”

He added: “The council house building announcement is certainly not going to help the situation.”

Explaining the link to Brexit, he said: “One of the biggest factors of that was ultimately Covid and Brexit, the perfect storm, seeing many skilled and qualified scaffolders that had been within the UK, leaving to go home. Then, of course, the changes around the exit of the Europe Union resulted in people not being able to return easily back to the United Kingdom, so as a result we've, we've got a significant shortage of very skilled scaffolders.”

Europe: The Way Back We’re campaigning to rebuild Britain’s future in Europe JOIN US HERE

He also noted that stringent, high level qualifications needed in the industry means that it takes five years to qualify as a scaffolder, meaning that training up new people will not fill vacancies in the short term.

Scaffolding is involved with multiple areas including home building and theatre productions, and already the petrochemical and offshore industries are struggling to recruit workers to do it.

Marley Morris, associate director for migration, trade and communities at the Institute of Public Policy for the Regions (IPPR), agreed that the construction industry had been particularly hit by shortages since Brexit.

Its 2017 report on the impact of Brexit, during the negotiations for Britain leaving the EU, warned that the UK would need to invest in skilled workers in the construction industry but that has failed to happen.

He noted that the end of free movement had been temporarily mitigated against by a “more liberal migration policy” in the first few years after Brexit but now that the government is tightening up there are more problems.

He said: “It's quite striking that when the Migration Advisory Committee published their temporary shortage list it was dominated by construction roles.

“I think that reflects that many of the key strategic occupations are construction dominated, and that reflects the government's priorities and the kind of cross-cutting nature of construction.”

The warnings are also supported by data from a Federation of Master Builders survey, which showed that almost a fifth (18 per cent) of the 493 respondents said their workforce had decreased in the second half of 2025.

Of the roles the hardest to fill, almost a third (30 per cent) reported difficulty in finding carpenters, compared to 33 per cent in 2020. More than a quarter (29 per cent) had difficulty getting bricklayers, 23 per cent in getting plumbers and 22 per cent in getting roofers.

Other challenging vacancies to fill were electricians (21 per cent), plasterers (20 per cent) painters and decorators (16 per cent) and scaffolders (12 per cent).

Almost three-quarters (72 per cent) of firms said they were affected by a lack of skilled tradespeople in the second half of 2025, compared to 61 per cent in the first half. Shortages caused job delays for half of those questioned, with almost one in four (22 per cent) saying they had led to job cancellations.

According to the Skills Training Group, the number of skilled manual workers has shrunk significantly in many of the key occupations for homebuilding from a decade ago.

The body's trade trends report published five years ago found that there were 35 per cent fewer bricklayers in 2020 compared to 2005, 23 per cent fewer plasterers, 18 per cent fewer painters and decorators and 17 per cent fewer carpenters and joiners.

The crisis in skilled labour has seen Mr Burnham adopt recommendations on vocational training from former health secretary Alan Milburn putting it on a par with getting a degree at university.

A report by social enterprise group Places for People last year warned that 250,000 new apprenticeships are needed to solve the crisis.

It warned: “The UK construction industry is facing a severe skills shortage, with over 140,000 job vacancies stalling essential housing and infrastructure projects. Despite skilled trades – such as bricklaying, plumbing, and roofing – comprising 10 per cent of England’s workforce, demand far exceeds supply.

“By 2035, over one-third of construction workers will retire, worsening the crisis. This shortfall puts the UK government’s ambitious 1.3 million new homes target at serious risk. With over 159,000 children living in temporary housing, urgent action is needed to boost recruitment, training, and retention in the construction sector.”

A Conservative spokesman said: “Once again, Andy Burnham is making promises with no plan for delivery.

“The numbers behind this announcement don’t add up and the government have said nothing about the funding profile. And there are clearly major gaps in the workforce that will stop homes getting built.”

The government has been approached for comment.

The draw for the Carabao Cup third round takes place tonight as more teams from the Premier League, including current cup winners Manchester City, enter the competition and learn who they will face.

Most top-flight clubs, such as Chelsea and Tottenham, entered the tournament in the second round with those who are competing in European competitions this season now involved as well.

Arsenal, Liverpool and Manchester United are among those to enter at this stage.

Their participation also means that the third round will be played across two midweeks in order for the teams involved in the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League to juggle their match schedules.

Here’s everything you need to know about the draw:

When is the Carabao Cup third round draw?

The draw for the Carabao Cup third round will take place on Wednesday 26 August. It will follow the conclusion of the second round tie between Preston and Everton which kicks off at 8pm BST, meaning the draw could start at around 10.15pm BST.

How will the draw work?

Pre-draw

Before the main draw, there is a pre-draw to decide if the eight Champions League and Europa League Clubs will be at home or away. This part is before Preston North End’s Round Two tie against Everton on Sky Sports.

Main draw

The main draw will take place following the conclusion of Round Two tie, the first eight ties will involve those Champions League and Europa League Clubs. Their home or away position will have already having been decided. They will then be drawn against a team in a separate bowl with the remaining teams in the competition.

Following the conclusion of those eight ties being drawn, the final eight ties will be drawn as normal.

From Round Three onwards, there is no longer a divide between the Northern and Southern sections.

How can I watch the Carabao Cup draw?

The Carabao Cup third-round draw will be shown live on Sky Sports Main Event and Sky Sports Football following the conclusion of Preston v Everton. The Independent understands a pre-draw show will happen before the game and the draw will take place after the final whistle.

Sky Sports subscribers will also be able to watch the draw live online via the Sky Go app.

Which teams are involved?

32 teams are involved in the draw including 23 winners of second round ties and nine additional Premier League clubs who are also competing in European competitions this season.

Those teams in Europe and entering the competition for the first time this season are: Arsenal, Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brighton & Hove Albion, Crystal Palace, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Sunderland.

Brighton & Hove Albion can also be in Europe through the UEFA Conference League, but that competition does not begin until October, so it does not affect the Round Three schedule.

What happens with the pre-draw?

Before the main draw, there will be a pre-draw to decide whether each of the eight Champions League and Europa League clubs will be at home or away. This will take place during the build-up to Preston vs Everton.

Organisers say this is to enable the Carabao Cup to proceed within its agreed schedule without disrupting other league or domestic cup fixtures amid a congested schedule for those in European competitions. It means that England’s eight European representatives cannot meet one another at this stage.

Carabao Cup draw ball numbers

The ball numbers will be confirmed on this morning ahead of the draw.

When will the Carabao Cup third round be played?

The third round of the Carabao Cup is scheduled to take place across consecutive weeks, starting on 7 September and 14 September. The ties will be played midweek as single-leg fixtures with the winners progressing to the fourth round.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers show promise of star double act for Chelsea
News.content:
“I am very happy for Cole,” Alonso said. “I have really enjoyed seeing him play with the dynamism and the freedom and the responsibility... when Cole feels this way we have a better team and a better Cole.”

Palmer makes it look very easy in this form, capable of switching the direction of play a beat before anyone else spots the opportunity. He and his old Manchester City academy friend Rogers came off before the end, Palmer having demonstrated some discomfort chasing a ball. Asked afterwards how ready he felt, Palmer responded in kind. “Did you not watch the game? I’m only joking, I’m ready... it was a difficult season with injuries and whatnot, but through the summer and since I’ve been back I’ve worked extra hard.”

If there was an attacker to compare with him on the other side it was King, who looks even better. The 19-year-old was way ahead of Arbeloa’s two young Real Madrid imports. García toiled away and took his chance, but César Palacios struggled for any impact in a position tucked in on the left. Oscar Bobb and King gave Fulham some edge but the concern, as ever, will be where Fulham get their goals.

Arbeloa pushed his full-backs high and encouraged Sander Berge to drop deep to get on the ball in the first passing phase. The Norwegian delayed too long in challenging João Pedro for Chelsea’s third – backing off and allowing Palmer to overlap to receive the pass.

Sánchez had not been the only concern for Chelsea. Back in the team, Levi Colwill misjudged a challenge on King in the first half and was relieved that the card was only yellow. Roméo Lavia took a wild swing at Calvin Bassey and was also booked. Moisés Caicedo was not fit to play. Enzo Fernández was on the bench and would come on in the second half to the kind of reception from opposition fans to which he will quickly become familiar.

There was a grin from the Argentine at those who berated him from the home stands when he returned at half-time. Fernández worked hard to transmit a general sense that the abuse did not land, although he will be relieved that the Chelsea fans were supportive. His future still feels very much in play.

It was Palmer’s subtle ball through that gave João Pedro the chance with 32 seconds of the game played. The ball came forward immediately from Lacroix’s firm header from defence. The Frenchman delivered a very accomplished assist for Rogers’s first-half goal. Before that King had equalised. There was an exchange with Timothy Castagne, and King looked up just inside the box and decided to have a swing at it. Sánchez was close enough to grasp the ball and somehow failed to do so.

Sánchez would later push a Castagne shot in the direction of García, who stooped and nodded the ball over the goalkeeper after Palmer had scored Chelsea’s third. This second error was unfortunate, but it is the kind of thing that happens to a goalkeeper as erratic as the one for whom Chelsea’s hierarchy seem to have such patience.

News.title: This summer’s wildfire epidemic is one of the worst in decades – so why are deaths so low?
News.content:
Wildfires in Britain and Europe this year are among the worst in decades, yet direct deaths are at some of the lowest levels, according to a Telegraph analysis.

As of early August, 505,683 hectares of land have burned across Europe, forcing the evacuation of more than 360,000 people as uncontrollable flames reach major cities, towns, and villages.

The problem is global – in the US, Nevada declared a state of emergency over the weekend after a wildfire caused more than 42,000 people to evacuate their homes.

But what sets 2026 apart isn’t just the vast areas of land burned, but how few deaths have been caused by the fires.

This summer, just 14 people are reported to have died in European wildfires, the vast majority in a single blaze in Almería, southern Spain.

By comparison, more than 130 people were killed in the summer of 2017 – a toll driven largely by the Pedrógão Grande disaster in Portugal, where more than 60 people died on a single stretch of road.

In 2018, at least 100 others died in a single afternoon in the Mati disaster near Athens, despite total hectares burned that year being roughly a third of current levels.

Since the modern phenomenon of summer wildfires exploded in Europe a decade ago, the direct death toll has broadly trended downward, as the chart below shows.

News.title: Swine flu outbreak in Delhi swamps clinics and hospitals
News.content:
India is battling a surge in H1N1 flu infections, prompting the federal health ministry to step up surveillance and hospital preparedness.

The national capital New Delhi has recorded 1,777 cases this year, almost eight times the number (229) reported during the same period in 2025.

Dr Randeep Guleria, a senior pulmonologist and director of Medanta Medical School, Gurugram, says the H1N1 cases are much higher than reported.

“It’s quite likely that the reported numbers are an underestimate because they depend on how many people are tested,” Guleria said. “If you speak to patients admitted to hospital who test positive for H1N1, you often find that other members of their family have similar symptoms, although they have not been tested.”

“There is a surge and we are seeing a lot of patients. We are testing only those who come to hospital and are more seriously ill,” Guleria said.

H1N1, commonly known as swine flu, is a subtype of influenza A. It is a contagious respiratory infection that can cause fever and cough and in severe cases it can lead to pneumonia and respiratory failure.

Officials at the Indian Council of Medical Research said the rise did not mean the emergence of a new strain of the virus.

The surge comes during India’s rainy season, when seasonal influenza and other respiratory infections typically increase.

Doctors in Delhi say they are seeing more patients with high fevers, persistent coughs and flu-like symptoms, although most cases remain mild.

The H1N1 cases have been reported beyond New Delhi. The metro cities like Mumbai, Chennai and Bangaluru have reported a high number of cases, although the pattern is not uniform across the country.

Doctors in Bangaluru have reported more influenza A infections among children, with some developing pneumonia and respiratory distress.

India’s health minister JP Nadda said there was a need for continued vigilance and robust surveillance. He has asked officials to monitor unusual increases and clusters of cases and ensure hospitals could respond quickly.

“Swine flu (H1N1) can show up through symptoms such as fever, cough, sore throat, headache, runny nose, body aches and fatigue… If you experience these symptoms, seek medical advice at your nearest healthcare centre,” the health ministry said on X.

Delhi’s health minister, Pankaj Kumar Singh, said the capital had enough beds, doctors, medicines and medical equipment to manage the increase. “Delhi is fully prepared to deal with the present health situation,” Singh said.

India has had several waves of H1N1 since the virus emerged globally in 2009.

The infection, commonly called swine flu, became a recurring seasonal respiratory illness after the 2009 pandemic rather than disappearing from circulation.

India recorded 3,320 H1N1 cases and 14 deaths in 2025, according to Ministry of Health data.

News.title: Newcastle and Liverpool serve up thrilling tribute to Kevin Keegan
News.content:
It is fitting that Newcastle United vs Liverpool is a Premier League opening weekend fixture following the death of Kevin Keegan at the age of 75 last month.

All corners of St James’ Park will pay tribute and show their appreciation for the former player and manager who means a great deal to both sets of supporters.

Fans will find a printed message from the Keegan family on the back of black and white cards on their seat, which they will hold up to display a mural before kick-off.

As well as playing for both clubs, Keegan was Newcastle’s manager when they were beaten by a last-gasp Stan Collymore goal at Anfield in April 1996, a 4-3 defeat remembered as one of the great Premier League games.

This fixture usually delivers entertainment, and with new managers Matthias Jaissle and Andoni Iraola promising front-footed, ‘vertical’ football, there should be goals. That was certainly the case last August, when Newcastle fought back from two down with 10 men, before Rio Ngumoha scored a memorable winner.

It has been a summer of tumult for Newcastle, losing manager Eddie Howe, as well as key players Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and captain Bruno Guimaraes. There has been bullish talk of “Newcastle 2.0” from David Hopkinson, the club’s chief executive, and the club believe they have found a promising coach, but fans have understandably revised expectations downwards.

Liverpool are a difficult team to read; champions only 18 months ago but brittle last season, which resulted in Arne Slot’s dismissal. Iraola’s appointment is a shift back towards Jurgen Klopp’s style. That will be music to the ears of Anfield regulars, but holes remain in the squad. Central midfield has not been replenished; they need a Mohamed Salah replacement, and their strength at full-back is questionable. Much will depend on how 21-year-old central defender Jérémy Jacquet fares alongside Vigin van Dijk but he impressed in pre-season.

Sports.title: Inside Cole Palmer’s amazing lifestyle, from £4.3million Surrey mansion to influencer girlfriend and Burberry contract
Sports.content:
WHAT a difference a summer off makes.

Cole Palmer put on a masterclass for Chelsea on Monday Night Football, scoring and grabbing an assist in a 3-2 win over Fulham.





That came after he was cruelly snubbed by Thomas Tuchel for England’s World Cup squad.

But, instead of wallowing in self-pity, the Blues playmaker enjoyed some downtime with pals in Ibiza, where he was spotted partying with Wayne Lineker at his Ocean Beach club.

And that’s just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to Palmer’s amazing lifestyle off the pitch.

He lives in a stunning £4.3million mansion in Surrey, dates a beautiful influencer, and even caught the eye of fashion giants Burberry, who signed him up on a modelling contract.

There’s absolutely nothing ‘Cold’ about his existence.

Mansion fit for a king

Like many Chelsea footballers, Cole 24, resides in the leafy Surrey Village of Oxshott.

His home, worth £4.3million, is situated behind private gated grounds.

It boasts six bedrooms, an expansive entrance hall and living room, as well as a modern kitchen and dining room.





While there’s also an entertainment room, where he can play video games and relax with friends after playing football.

Although his planning application to build an outdoor gym sparked objections from his neighbours.

Influencer Wag

Cole is currently dating the stunning blonde model and influencer, Olivia Holder, dubbed the ‘Pilates Princess’.

They were first spotted together last December enjoying a date at London’s Winter Wonderland.

The 24-year-old stunner reportedly runs a beauty clinic alongside her sister in Bromley in Greater London.

A devout Christian, Olivia regularly discusses her faith on Instagram.

She is becoming the ultimate Chelsea Wag, and is often seen in the hospitality section at Stamford Bridge.

Olivia has enjoyed the trappings of Cole’s lifestyle, including luxury holidays in Dubai, Ibiza, Cannes, and Marbella.



Cars

When it comes to motors, Cole has a very impressive collection.

When he began life as a Man City trainee, his trusted car was a Volkswagen Polo.

But, now on a salary of £130,000-per-week, he’s been able to branch out to more luxurious brands.

The most impressive is his Lamborghini Urus, worth a whopping £190,000. It was customized by WRAPvehicles with neon green brake calipers and gloss black wheels.



He has added a BMW i4 M50 to his garage, worth around £72,000.

Cole also was seen behind the wheel of a reliable Mercedes-Benz A-Class, which starts at £31,000.

He’s in fashion

Thanks to his persona on the pitch, earning him the nickname ‘Cold Palmer’ because of his epic goal celebration, the midfielder has scored plenty of fans.

And many have taken to his fashion style too, dubbing it Palmercore – mixing high-street luxury brands with streetwear and tracksuits.

That said, he has rocked up to high-profile ceremonies like the PFA Awards and GQ Men of the Year events in designer suits and tuxedos, so he’s not always so paired down.

His style caught the attention of British fashion house Burberry, who signed him up on a seasonal campaign deal.

Cole went viral with a nine-minute fishing film for the brand called The Duffle with Cole Palmer.

Amusingly, the clip sees him sitting by a lake fishing in complete silence for the entire duration.



The playmaker also starred alongside Arsenal star Eberechi Eze for their It’s Always Burberry Weather campaign, where he wore Burberry’s classic coats and trademark knits.

Back in June, Cole was a cover star for trendy i-D Magazine in partnership with Burberry to model their latest collection.

There’s more to come…

All of this is brewing quite nicely to build Palmer into a brand.

Last October, Cole successfully trademarked the term ‘Cold Palmer’ with the UK government’s Intellectual Property Office.

What does that mean? Well, now no one can use his nickname for commercial purposes without first getting his permission first.

Second, he can now add that trademarked term to products he wants to endorse.

Think toys, clothes, footballs, football boots, and even food.

He also managed to trademark his name, autograph, and shivering goal celebration.



There is already a partnership with Gopuff who launched a premium ice brand they’ve aptly called COLE’D.

Expect more merch to follow.

Sports.title: Why Nicolas Jackson to Aston Villa transfer is so complicated despite Chelsea outcast and Emery being perfect match
Sports.content:
NICOLAS JACKSON going to Aston Villa would make sense for everyone.

Chelsea want him off their books, Villa need a striker, and Jackson and Unai Emery would love to be reunited after their spell together at Villarreal.



But multiple factors, from Uefa’s “45-day rule” and Premier League loan regulations, to the intrigue surrounding Julian Alvarez’s future at Atletico Madrid, are putting spanners in the works.

Which is why Villa, after shadowing Jackson most of the summer, are now looking at other options, such as Crystal Palace’s wantaway frontman Jean-Philippe Mateta.



And why Chelsea, for the second summer in a row, find themselves scrambling to find Jackson a new home, preferably a permanent one.

Despite the fact the Senegal striker would be a more natural replacement for Ollie Watkins, if he joins the Villa exodus, than Mateta.



Chelsea and Villa have already done business this summer. Morgan Rogers moved to Stamford Bridge for £117m, a record for a British player, in late July.

Soon afterwards, Alejandro Garnacho moved in the other direction, on loan with a conditional buy clause.

But those deals make a Jackson move more difficult and less attractive for both clubs.

Under Uefa rules, if clubs sell players to each other within a 45-day period they are treated as a player swap – not as two separate transactions.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

In those circumstances, the clubs are not able to put any profit on the player they have sold directly on to their books for accounting purposes.

The rules are complex, but the upshot is the selling clubs cannot enjoy the full benefit of the agreed fee when it comes to calculations related to Uefa and PL financial rules.

Rogers’ transfer to Chelsea was confirmed on July 21. So if Jackson were to move in the other direction before the window closes next Tuesday, the deal would fall within the 45-day window.

The result would be Villa not being able to add all the profit on Rogers to their accounts and Chelsea facing the same restriction on what they received for Jackson.



The Uefa regulations allow wriggle room if players move initially on loan, although there are still restrictions.

But that option is not open to Chelsea and Villa. PL rules say clubs can only have one player on loan from another PL club at any one time. And Garnacho is already filling that slot at Villa Park.

An added complication is Villa and Chelsea are already in Uefa’s bad books for breaching regulations.

They are operating under settlement agreements which set them financial targets they must meet to avoid further fines and punishment.



Villa have already sold Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Ezri Konsa to help balance the books. Ollie Watkins wants to follow them out by making a lucrative move to Saudi Arabia.

Jackson would be much more of a direct replacement for Watkins than a player like Mateta.

Although Chelsea are not involved in European competition this season, they still have to meet most of the terms of their settlement.

The Blues seem to be pretty cool right now about the Jackson situation, because of interest from other clubs. But Atletico seem like the best bet.



The LaLiga side have been in talks with the Blues on and off the whole summer.

Director of football Mateu Alemany was in London earlier this month.

But Atletico have, until now, been pushing for an initial loan deal for Jackson.

And Chelsea, after another busy summer of incomings, would much prefer a permanent deal.



They value the 25-year-old at £65m. Jackson arrived three years ago for £30m on an eight-year contract.

Which means his current value for accounting purposes, after allowing for amortisation, is just under £20m. So a £65m fee would bring a profit of more than £45m.

The trick will be finding someone willing to pay that much, either up front or as a compulsory purchase after an initial loan.

Atletico have so far resisted. But their own problems with Alvarez are coming to a head.



The Argentinian star has been pushing for a move, preferably to Barcelona, all summer.

The start of the new season has upped the stakes, with Alvarez being booed by Atletico fans and a toxic atmosphere developing.

It would be a major climbdown by Atletico if they sold their star player, after insisting he would be staying.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They were already looking at Jackson because of an injury to Alexander Sorloth. But if Alvarez left, the need for reinforcements up front on a longer-term basis would become critical.

All of which leaves Jackson in limbo, waiting to see if all the different rules and all the other transfer sagas will align for him to get his move away.

Sports.title: Man Utd CONFIRM £70million Carlos Baleba transfer from Brighton as Seagulls insert genius contract clause
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have announced the £70million signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton.

The Cameroon international, 22, has penned a five-year deal at Old Trafford with the option of a further 12 months.



And his arrival for £65m plus £5m in add-ons should round off the Red Devils’ relentless midfield spending spree.

United bosses had already splurged £50m on Andrey Santos from Chelsea and £35m on Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa.





But they wanted a third to sure up Michael Carrick‘s squad after Casemiro‘s move to Inter Miami and Manuel Ugarte‘s long-term knee injury.

And they teased the announcement with a tweet at 4.30pm on Tuesday.

The club simply wrote: “#areyouareabaleba” which sent United fans into ecstasy.

They then replied to their own post with a video of Baleba in the red home shirt saying: “Hi, I’m a Baleba.”



The official confirmation of the deal, including photos of the midfielder putting pen to paper, dropped at 4.45pm.

Baleba said: “It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

“I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick – his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

“The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.”



Jason Wilcox, director of football, added: “Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further.

“He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

“We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.

“Carlos’ determination to join Manchester United and his confidence that we will achieve our shared ambitions mean that he is the perfect signing as we continue to build a dynamic and entertaining team ready to compete across multiple competitions.”

The fact the Red Devils have almost halved the £120m price tag they were quoted for Baleba last summer will come as some relief.



Brighton have covered their backs by inserting a sell-on clause which could bump up their earnings from the deal if United cash in down the line.

Last season was not the youngster’s finest on the South Coast as he managed only 35 goalless appearances in all competitions.

But United were long-standing admirers of Baleba, and they hope he can compete with Santos, Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo for the two deep-lying midfield spots in Carrick’s starting line-up.



The new recruit can also play at left-back, where United may need cover for Luke Shaw during a long season of domestic and European football.

Baleba has been nursing an ankle injury and is not expected to return until mid-September.

He scored four times in 112 appearances for Brighton after they snapped him up from Lille as a 19-year-old for £23.2m.

Hos last appearance for the Seagulls, ironically, came against Carrick’s United on the final day of last season.

Sports.title: Aston Villa set to complete stunning Leon Goretzka transfer as Champions League winner, 31, passes medical
Sports.content:
ASTON VILLA are set to complete the signing of Leon Goretzka on a free transfer.

And the Villans are also keen on recruiting Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta before next week’s transfer deadline.



Unai Emery‘s side are desperate to add to their squad following Sunday’s 4-0 drubbing at Brighton.

According to reporter Florian Plettenberg, the German international has completed his medical and will soon be announced as a Villa player.



Emery is said to have phoned Goretzka in a bid to convince him to join.

The former Bayern Munich star, 31, is expected to be pen a multi-year contract.



Goretzka had been a free agent since leaving Bayern at the end of last season.

The experienced midfielder remained a regular at Allianz Arena last season prior to his release, making 31 Bundesliga appearances and 48 in all competitions.

Goretzka signed for Bayern from Schalke in 2018 and played 312 times for the Bavarian giants, scoring 51 goals and laying on 53 assists.

He contributed to several trophy wins, including seven league titles and a Champions League.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Villa lost key midfielder Youri Tielemans to Manchester United last month, while Amadou Onana is set to be a long-term absentee with a knee injury.

Emery started Sunday’s thrashing at Brighton with Boubacar Kamara, Ross Barkley and Joao Gomes in midfield, the latter being sent off.

In addition to midfield, the Midlands club also want to bolster their forward line amid Ollie Watkins‘ mooted move to Saudi Arabia.

Earlier today it emerged that Villa have made an offer to sign Crystal Palace striker Mateta.



The bid is said to have been worth around £25million and was turned down by the Eagles.

Palace are claimed to want around £40m, despite Mateta’s contract being set to expire.

And the Villans are also considering swoops for Rafael Leao and Nicolas Jackson as the deadline approaches.

Sports.title: Arsenal strike transfer deal to sign wonderkid goalie, 15, with THREE more prodigies to come including Man Utd duo
Sports.content:
ARSENAL have continued their academy recruitment drive by agreeing a deal for Northern Ireland wonderkid Phoenix Blayney.

The goalkeeper, 15, will join the club next summer from Larne FC and be part of the Gunners’ scholarship intake for the 2027-28 season.



Blayney has also signed a pre-contract agreement to pen pro terms with Arsenal when he turns 17 in November next year.

The teenager has been tipped for a bright future and has already represented Northern Ireland at Under-17 level.



The Gunners have made a point of boosting their academy ranks with new signings to improve results.

The club are hoping to agree three more deals this week to bolster their Under-21 squad for the new season.

Manchester United duo James Scanlon and Habeeb Ogunneye are set to arrive, as is Blackburn striker Igor Tyjon.

Work is also being done to bring in striker Vincent Joseph, 16, after he rejected the chance to pen pro terms with Liverpool.

Midfielder Axel Donczew, the youngest player to ever represent Cardiff, has already agreed to join the club.

And striker Mylo Bernard, who is also 16, is making his way to the Emirates after rejecting the opportunity to continue his development with Crystal Palace.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Arsenal have made big changes to the academy this summer, with Pascal De Maesschalck now running the show.

The Belgian replaced Per Mertesacker, who left at the end of last season, and reports into sporting director Andrea Berta.

Sports.title: Chelsea legend QUITS England role after five years after landing ill-fated first role in management
Sports.content:
ASHLEY COLE has quit his England under-21 role after five years.

And SunSport understands he made the decision months before his ill-fated first job in management.



The Chelsea legend stepped down from his position with the young Lions in March before taking charge of Italian side Cesena.

The FA has now confirmed Cole will not return to his role with England.



His departure comes after the 45-year-old ended his short-lived spell as Cesena boss following just eight games in charge.

Cole landed his first managerial job with the Serie B club in March, having previously worked as part of the coaching staff at Everton and Derby.

But after just three months at the helm, he decided to walk away following discussions with Cesena’s sporting director over a change in the club’s strategy.

Cole announced his departure on Instagram.

He wrote: “As my tenure at Cesena FC concludes today, I want to thank the players and staff for their hard work and commitment over the last few months.

“I was proud to bring my experience to such a passionate club, and I’ve truly enjoyed working with the squad to introduce a new identity and prepare for the season ahead.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“Following recent discussions with the Sporting Director regarding a change in the club’s strategy, I have decided that it is best for me to move on.

“I leave with great respect for all the people there, as well as the fans, and look forward to my next challenge.”

Cole signed a short-term contract with Cesena when he took over in March, with the option to extend if he met “certain conditions”.

But his first spell in management proved a major struggle.

He managed just one victory during his eight games in charge, alongside three draws and four defeats.



His appointment was met with a mixed reaction from Cesena supporters, while there were also reports of unrest among some players.

Cole also admitted he had struggled with the language barrier after moving to Italy.

The former Arsenal and Chelsea full-back had previously spent two years in Italy as a player with Roma, making 16 appearances for the club.

His latest managerial setback leaves him looking for his next opportunity after a career that saw him establish himself as one of the greatest full-backs of his generation.



Cole made almost 400 Premier League appearances and won 107 England caps during a glittering playing career.

He also enjoyed two spells with Chelsea, winning multiple major trophies including the Champions League and Premier League.

Sports.title: Man Utd complete Baleba signing
Sports.content:
Manchester United have completed the signing of midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton.

The Cameroon international, 22, joins the club in a deal worth up to £70m, made up of a £65m guaranteed fee plus £5m in add-ons.

He has signed a five-year contract which includes the option of a further year.

Baleba is currently injured having picked up an ankle injury in pre-season, but Sky Sports News understands he could be back by mid-September. Manchester United play Manchester City on September 13, live on Sky Sports.

Baleba's arrival at Old Trafford brings an end to a transfer saga that has lasted almost 12 months. Sky Sports News has been reporting on United's interest in Baleba since last autumn and broke the news that they enquired about signing him during the January transfer window.

He remained one of United's top targets this summer and becomes their third addition in midfield after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

"It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour," Baleba told the club's website.

"I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

"The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together."

Baleba joined Brighton from Lille in 2023 and made 112 appearances for the club. He featured 35 times last season and was absent for a spell while representing Cameroon at the Africa Cup of Nations.

Is Baleba a major gamble or a game-changer for Man Utd?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look as Sky Sports' William Bitibiri explains exactly what Carlos Baleba might bring to Manchester United's midfield

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

A year ago, Carlos Baleba appeared to have the world at his feet.

A breakout season at Brighton had established the then-21-year-old as one of the Premier League's most coveted young midfielders, with a move to one of Europe's elite clubs seemingly inevitable. Manchester United were among those interested, having identified Baleba as a potential transformative presence in midfield.

But Brighton's reported £100m-plus valuation proved a stumbling block. The move never materialised and Baleba stayed at the Amex.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at Carlos Baleba's Premier League best bits

His form subsequently dipped dramatically. His numbers fell and, at times, he looked a shadow of the midfielder who had generated so much excitement the previous season.

That makes this a gamble for United. But, stylistically, there are few midfielders better suited to what they need.

Image: Baleba was among the league's leading defensive midfielders during the 2024/25 season - can he revive that form?

United require greater authority in the middle of the pitch and, crucially, someone capable of winning the ball back in deeper areas. Baleba brings exactly that. His athleticism, aggression and ability to carry the ball through midfield would add a level of dynamism and steel that is currently missing.

Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans have been astute additions, but Baleba offers something different: specialist defensive power coupled with the athleticism to drive United up the pitch.

His age is another major factor. Baleba is still only 22 and, despite his inconsistent season, there remains a belief around him that he can develop into one of the world's best midfielders.

That ambition is reflected in his influences. Baleba has spoken of his admiration for Paul Pogba, Yaya Toure and Andres Iniesta, while Neymar and Ronaldinho were among his favourite players to watch. There is a desire for self-expression in his game that goes beyond the physical qualities that made so highly rated.

There is risk attached to signing him. United would be betting on the player Baleba can become rather than simply the one he has been over the past 12 months.

But if United want to find a midfielder capable of growing into one of the best in his position, this is exactly the sort of gamble they should be willing to take.

Sports.title: Warren thinks Fury-AJ fight will go ahead in America
Sports.content:
Frank Warren says he thinks a long-awaited heavyweight showdown between Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua will go ahead in America despite claims the bout is in doubt.

Everything seemed to be in place for the British pair of former world champions to meet in London in November, but Saudi organisers Sela's desire to instead hold the event in the USA has created a hold up.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn has been pushing to keep the fight in London, which led to Fury claiming last week that the contest was in "serious doubt" because his rival was asking for "more money".

However, Fury's promoter Warren has allayed fears the fight could be called off, and insists The Gypsy King would also have preferred it to take place in the UK.

Warren told Sky Sports News: "I genuinely think it will happen. His Excellency, Turki Al-Alsheikh, he will announce that fairly soon.

"I know there's been some issues with contracts with Matchroom and AJ; I believe they will iron all those out.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Eddie Hearn claimed that Anthony Joshua feels a responsibility to UK fight fans that AJ vs Fury should happen in the UK.

"In the meantime, Tyson [Fury] has flown off to the States, he's in Miami and he's preparing for the fight.

"I think they both want the fight at Wembley, but it's out of their hands now. That's not quite right, actually, they could refuse to fight. We don't get the fight we want to see.

"I think because of the amount of money involved, I hope I'm wrong, but I think it will go on in America."

'Nothing unusual' for all-British clash to take place abroad

Warren says the fight taking place outside of the UK would be "nothing unusual" in terms of boxing's history.

"You had two massive American heroes in Muhammad Ali and George Foreman," Warren said. "Two American fighters, all the Americans wanted to see it, Vegas wanted to put the fight on, Madison Square Gardens wanted to see it, and it went off to Zaire.

"Everybody thought: 'What on earth was that all about?' But it became not just an iconic fight and an iconic moment in sport.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tyson Fury doesn't hold back as he lashes out at Anthony Joshua as the wait goes on for the pair to confirm a much-anticipated showdown. Credit: @tysonfury.

"Ali had the 'Thrilla in Manila' with Joe Frazier. Joe Bugner fought Ali in Kuala Lumpur, it's nothing unusual.

"I think it's like all sportsmen, say, for example, David Beckham, he went off and played at the end of his career [abroad], and he did that because of the money.

"And that's why these guys are doing this, they are professional boxers.

"Would I like to see it at Wembley? Would all the fans like to see it at Wembley? Of course they would. But they are in the hands of another broadcaster who wants the fight in America."

Sports.title: What is the reality of Villa's finances ahead of Deadline Day?
Sports.content:
All of this is a far cry from the euphoria of Istanbul in May, and that is what adds to the feeling of bemusement about how significant the changes have been to Aston Villa's squad and how quickly it has occurred.

Last season was their most successful since 1982, when they won the old European Cup.

This time round, it was a Europa League win and a fourth-place Premier League finish - each of those achievements would have been enough to guarantee the riches and prestige of Champions League football.

Unai Emery was lauded as a hero by Villa fans even before last spring's spectacular, and rightly so.

He has won the Europa League title five times with three different clubs. A key question now is whether his downbeat assessment following the humbling by Brighton is indicative of a wider concern.

Clearly, Emery was upset with Ollie Watkins, and it currently seems a tall order for the striker to be reintegrated into the Villa squad, having made his desire to leave clear.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Unai Emery was short of words when asked about the future of Ollie Watkins and then after the match said to find out we should call the striker

But more worrying is the overriding sense that Emery is struggling with the lack of options he has at his disposal right now.

After all that he has achieved at the club, his reward has been widespread disruption within the squad after four key player departures, potentially more to come, and limited finances.

Emery described it as having "had an intelligent market", amid efforts by the club to strengthen the squad before the deadline. "We know where we are and we know what we want to do again for the next year," he said.

There is mitigation for Villa's bosses, however, who have been frustrated by PSR rules, which they feel have been an ambition killer and stalled their progress.

The switch to Squad Cost Ratio (SCR) rules this season has only added to that and caused deeper resentment.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports explains the new financial Squad Cost Ratio rules that Premier League clubs will have to adhere to this season

As regulars in European competition now, they are limited to spending 70 per cent of their football revenue on transfer fees and player wages.

Remember, they have already been fined twice by UEFA recently, being hit with a £9.5m penalty last year and a £19.4m fine in June, although £13m of that was suspended after Villa came to a settlement agreement.

That means, inevitably, Villa are a club that has to generate income from player trading in order to buy new talent.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher discuss the outgoings of Aston Villa this transfer window and how much of an impact this could have on their season

The proof of that is in the figures from sales over the last three years; Villa have made over £410m selling the likes of Douglas Luiz, Jhon Duran, Jacob Ramsey and Moussa Diaby, before this summer's sale of Morgan Rogers, Ezri Konsa, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne.

Should Emiliano Martinez and Ollie Watkins follow, that number will be close to the half-a-billion mark, in terms of funds generated.

It is a big ask for Emery to see the castle that he has built taken down keystone by keystone, knowing he has to rebuild again. Last summer, the transfer upheaval contributed to the director of football Monchi leaving the club.

Importantly, Villa currently feel confident their manager is secure. After all, his contract has another three seasons to run, following the bumper new five-year deal he signed in May 2024.

But many of the biggest clubs in Europe have noticed with admiration the job Emery has done at Villa Park, and he will always be on the shortlist of the top clubs for as long as he keeps doing such a stellar job under the circumstances.

Sports.title: 'Stupid mistakes' - Root 'hacked off' by latest off-field incident
Sports.content:
A furious Joe Root vowed England would earn back the trust of the nation after his return as Test captain was overshadowed by the latest off-field incident to rock English cricket.

England swept Pakistan away by an innings and 103 runs inside three days at Headingley to hand Root victory on his comeback as Test captain.

Within 24 hours, video footage emerged of England fast bowler Brydon Carse being handcuffed and led away by police on Saturday night after Durham's players had gone out to celebrate their win at Derbyshire in the County Championship.

Carse, who was seen talking to team-mate Matthew Potts, with former England captain Ben Stokes also pictured in the background, has subsequently been withdrawn from the squad for the second Pakistan Test at Lord's with an investigation by the Cricket Regulator underway.

"If I'm being brutally honest, I'm really hacked off," Root told a press conference. "I'm really disappointed that after last week's performance we are sat here and we're talking about something not related to it at all.

"In terms of the incident itself, obviously with the regulator, there's not a lot I can say on it. It's in their hands now.

"I've spoken to Brydon when I first found out; my first concern was for him as a person. In my time in the dressing room, you obviously develop personal relationships with players.

"I don't think I'm speaking out of turn when I say he's been very upset and has been very apologetic and understands his actions. I'm sure when he gets his chance, he will say that himself.

Image: Carse was seen in handcuffs outside a nightclub in Derby

"It's not the isolated incident itself, it's the fact that we continually keep making stupid mistakes away from the game and it's detracting from what we're doing on the field."

The Carse incident is not the first off-field episode England have had to navigate.

White-ball captain Harry Brook was punched by a bouncer while out the evening before a one-day international in New Zealand last autumn.

An unverified video appeared to show opener Ben Duckett drunk while the team were on a mid-series break in the beach resort of Noosa during their ill-fated Ashes tour.

Stokes and fast bowler Gus Atkinson missed the second Test of the 2-1 home defeat to New Zealand earlier this summer after breaking the curfew to attend a Chelsea nightclub as they celebrated victory in the first game of the series at Lord's.

Stokes and Atkinson were cleared of violent conduct but hit with written warnings after "breaching specific contractual obligations".

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the day three of the first Test between England and Pakistan as Joe Root's side cruised to an innings victory at Headingley.

'We have to earn a lot of trust back'

Asked if English cricket had an image problem, Root, who previously called for his players to "be adults" while announcing the removal of the curfew, said: "We have an opportunity going forward.

"Clearly we're not portraying ourselves as we want to. We've got an opportunity to build a culture that is very strong and we can be proud of that's player-driven.

"That's not going to happen overnight. We've had conversations about what is expected from us, what it means and takes to play for England.

"We want to create something we can be proud of, what people following us can be proud of. We want supporters to look at us and revere, not just what we do on the field but off it as well.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, Michael Atherton and Nasser Hussain praise England's winning fast bowler combinations during the three-day victory over Pakistan in first Test.

"Over the next little while, as leader of this team, with Stephen [Fleming], and with the group of players as well, is creating something that is just that."

Root continued: "We have a chance to build something that lives alongside what we achieved last week on the field. I thought it was a brilliant performance. The way we played was exceptional.

"We have to align that with being exceptional off the field as well and understand what that looks like and how we want to represent ourselves and our nation.

"With what we've got coming up, there are plenty of opportunities to do that. But like I say, it's not going to happen overnight, in many ways we're going to have to earn a lot of trust back.

"And something we're going to have to live and breathe consistently."

Sports.title: Baumgardner to face undefeated Turhan as blockbuster Dubois showdown nears
Sports.content:
Alycia Baumgardner will move up a division to fight Elif Nur Turhan for her IBF lightweight world title on November 8 in a seismic move that brings a blockbuster showdown with Caroline Dubois a step closer.

Baumgardner, the reigning unified WBO, WBA and IBF super featherweight world champion, will jump up five pounds to the 135lbs division to face the undefeated Turhan in the headline bout of MVPW-07 at College Park Center in Arlington, Texas.

"When I set my mind to something, I see it through, and 135 will be no different," Baumgardner said. "This is a super fight, the kind of fight boxing deserves, and the beginning of my next chapter.

"I know what it takes to become undisputed. I've done it before, and I'll do it again."

Turhan added: "Alycia is a boxer who steps into the ring determined to win, never even entertaining the possibility of defeat. I know I am facing an opponent who steps into the ring solely for victory.

"I do not want to lose either. As two boxers sharing a 'win at all costs' mentality, we guarantee a fierce, relentless battle where everything is left on the line. Two warriors, one fight and only one winner."

Victory for Baumgardner would see her become a two-weight world champion in the same division as Dubois, who holds the WBC and WBO titles.

The 32-year-old is set to be ringside for Dubois' clash with Amelia Moore on Saturday, live on Sky Sports.

Since December, Dubois has been vociferous in calling out Baumgardner, and those calls have only intensified since she beat Terri Harper to unify the division in April.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Baumgardner dismissed the prospects of facing Caroline Dubois after her win over Bo Mi Re Shin. Instead, the fighter called out Katie Taylor and Amanda Serrano

Baumgardner has maintained that, despite her status as a unified world champion, Dubois has yet to reach the level required for her to entertain a fight between them.

But should Baumgardner inflict a first career defeat on Turhan, all roads will surely lead to a blockbuster unification bout with Dubois, where the winner would move to within one victory of becoming undisputed champion.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Dubois is determined to fight Baumgardner sooner rather than later

The co-main event on November 8 will see England's Ellie Scotney fight the undefeated Tiara Brown over 10 rounds for the WBC featherweight world title.

Former undisputed super bantamweight champion Scotney will step up to 126lbs as she bids to become a two-weight world champion.

"MVPW-07 is one of the biggest championship events in boxing history, with four back-to-back world title fights, bringing together eight elite fighters from around the world with belts at stake in every match-up," said Nakisa Bidarian and Jake Paul, co-founders of Most Valuable Promotions.

Sports.title: Manchester United confirm Carlos Baleba signing as midfield spend nears £150m
Sports.content:
Manchester United have completed the signing of the Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70m. The Cameroon international is the third midfielder to join this summer, after Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Baleba has signed a five-year-deal with the option to extend for 12 months after United agreed a £65m deal plus £5m in add-ons and a sell-on with Brighton. It takes the club’s spend on midfielders to about £148m.

Santos and Tielemans have arrived from Chelsea and Aston Villa respectively during a summer in which Casemiro has left and Manuel Ugarte sustained a serious knee injury.

“It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams,” Baleba said. “Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

“I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick. His experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

“The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.”

United made a move to bring in Baleba last summer but cooled their pursuit when Brighton made it abundantly clear he was not leaving. Baleba was not at his best last season but that did not put off United, who stepped up their interest in the 22-year-0ld a week ago.

United’s director of football, Jason Wilcoxm said: “Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further. He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Two goals, some polish and a rebrand: City flip Sávio for quite the profit
Sports.content:
BRAZILIAN WINGERS UNDER THE HAMMER

We see Manchester City have managed to flip Savinho for quite the profit. Football Daily had previously assumed this sort of wheeler-dealing was restricted to the Dion-Dublin-adjacent property market, or the Harry-Redknapp-infused used car scene, but it seems we were mistaken. We have no idea how City ended up trousering a £44.2m markup on a player who cost £30.8m two seasons ago, and has achieved the square root of eff all since, but they’ve done it. Consider standing stock still and allowing a ball to clank off you and into the net in an FA Cup tie at Newcastle analogous to installing a new bathroom suite and giving the front room a lick of paint, or taking a microfibre cloth and some polish to the crevices of that grimy dashboard. Result! Goal! Ker-ching! That’s 75 million-nil!

Spurs were the mark, and they could end up paying £85m if all the silverware-related add-ons kick in. So £75m it is, then. But that’s still a fair old whack for an attacking player who scored two goals for City in 53 league appearances. The 22-year-old Brazilian plays on the right flank, so will almost certainly take the place of Mikey Moore, who thought his day at Brentford last weekend had gone badly enough, only for his manager Roberto De Zerbi to go out of his way to namecheck him – and him alone, twice – in his post-match deconstruction of a 3-0 fiasco for which pretty much everyone wearing Tottenham’s traditional blue, gold and dayglo pink was culpable.

Upon signing, Savinho announced that he wishes to be known forthwith as Sávio, reverting to the monicker from his time at Girona, where he scored 11 goals and set up 10 others during a loan stint that was a damn sight more successful than his spell at the Etihad. It’s also his actual name, so there is that. Sávio is far from the first of his countrymen to toy with this most personal of brands – Brazil’s greatest-ever player was actually called Manuel Francisco dos Santos, and Pelé was the result of a name change too – and we’re pretty sure he won’t be the last. Spurs meanwhile will simply be hoping they’re getting the Girona version of their new purchase, because otherwise City will have, in more ways than one, properly flipped them off. Omar Marmoush – 16 goals in 62 appearances, brand-new kitchen worktops, shiny hubcaps – next!

Enough is enough” – a group of influential current and former footballers, including Mikaël Silvestre, Lucy Bronze, Emmanual Petit and David James, have piled more pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa. However the Cameroon Football Federation’s head-honcho and one-time unimpressed interviewee, Samuel Eto’o, dismissed criticism of Infantino’s leadership. “I don’t think that [he] has done anything wrong,” he honked. “I think the timing of all [the criticism] is because there’s an election coming out.”

Sports.title: WSL academy teams to play in third tier after FA approves controversial plan
Sports.content:
Four Women’s Super League academy sides will play in tier three of the pyramid from the 2027-28 season after the controversial proposal was approved by the Football Association’s board.

The change forms part of what the FA described as a package of reforms to the Women’s National League “designed to strengthen the women’s football pyramid, raise standards across the league, and improve the development pathway for young players”.

The FA said data showed that young English players were getting significantly fewer competitive minutes than their counterparts across Europe’s leading leagues.

Quick Guide How do I 

The FA said WNL clubs would receive central funding for the first time and that changes to the loan market would encourage clubs from the top two divisions to loan players to clubs in the third and fourth tiers.

The WSL academy teams will not be eligible for promotion and will be chosen against criteria to be developed in the coming months, the FA said. With the third tier split into two geographical regions, it is expected that two academies will be placed in the northern division and two in the southern.

Sue Day, director of women’s football at the FA, said: “For the game to continue moving forward, the FA Women’s National League must evolve alongside the professional game, and we need to create more opportunities for talented young English players to develop in senior football.”

Sports.title: ‘Enough is enough’: players pile pressure on under-fire Gianni Infantino to resign
Sports.content:
A group of influential current and former footballers have added to the pressure on Gianni Infantino by calling for change at the top of Fifa, saying “enough is enough” in a statement shared widely across social media.

The intervention is particularly significant given some of those behind its circulation have undertaken ambassadorial activities for Fifa as part of its “Fifa Legends” programme. Among them is the former Manchester United and Arsenal defender Mikaël Silvestre, who also sits on the governing body’s 16-member players’ voice panel designed to assist with anti-racism initiatives.

Others to have shared the statement include the England defender Lucy Bronze, the former England keeper David James and the France 1998 World Cup winner Emmanuel Petit. More signatories are expected to follow in a concerted reaction to Infantino’s ill-fated attempt to sell stakes in the World Cup.

“We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world,” part of the statement read. “Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under Fifa’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

Quick Guide Play our football trivia game, On the ball Show The Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues? Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.”

The group called for efforts to “reshape the future of our sport”, adding: “There are good people within Fifa who want to rebuild trust, but a new era requires a structured change: a real, direct say for players and fans in how football is run. Those who step on to the pitch and those who sit in the stands deserve a genuine voice to help reshape football’s future together.”

Infantino has resisted calls to resign and spent Saturday at a youth tournament in the Dominican Republic, attempting to smooth relations with some of the smaller Caribbean member associations on whose support his fate may hinge.

One former player with a different perspective on Infantino is the former Real Madrid, Barcelona and Chelsea striker Samuel Eto’o, who is president of the Cameroonian football federation. In an interview with CNN, Eto’o said Infantino had not committed any missteps and called for the Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme to be put back on the table if Infantino is re-elected next March. He said the money from FFE would “reset the balance of power” in football and ensure African countries avoided losing top players to other national teams.

“I don’t think that [Infantino] has done anything wrong,” he said. “All of this has happened because there’s an election coming out, that’s all there is.

“I want to see all of my colleagues, all of the presidents, re-reading the project. After president Infantino is re-elected, we will have the strength to ask for this project to be put back on the table for discussion. I remain convinced that, if there is a democratic vote, this project will be adopted because it’s good for the majority.”

Sports.title: Post-Pep Premier League era begins with blast of hyper-managed shock and awe | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
There has been something oddly narcotic and moreish about the drip‑drip of fresh Pep Guardiola content either side of the start of the new Premier League season. Eras come and go. Everything dies, baby, that’s a fact. But four‑part Amazon Prime documentaries make angels of us all.

So we have continued to feast on the Pep-at-City visuals: dead jeopardy, reheated beefs, the uplifting team talks of a departed manager to the departed players of a departed team, and moments that often feel far more gripping than the daily churn of what we must, out of habit, call the real world.

The thought occurred watching all this: has the Premier League found its Tupac? Is Pep just going to keep on doing this, dropping new material, fresh hits, posthumous platinum albums? A bald, thin charismatic man who keeps on releasing his lost tapes. We have exactly the thing, sir. Is he even actually dead?

Probably this won’t happen. But a profound absence is still a profound presence at moments like these. The ghosts continue to pull the strings. This weekend was the first of the new Premier League season. More significantly, it was also the first of the post‑Pep era.

And this has been a genuine era, 10 years in the game and an entire tactical culture shift in the making. Unsurprisingly, there was an odd sense of lightness across those nine fixtures on Friday through to Sunday, of old bonds cast aside, even a little giddiness. Suddenly dad isn’t home. The chair by the door is empty. Let’s all just rip it up a bit, shall we?

This relies on a slightly out‑of‑date notion of what Guardiola‑ism became in its later years. But the fact is, something interesting did happen in those Friday‑to‑Sunday games. Think of pure Pep-ball and what are you seeing? Possession. Cold, high‑craft control. This is a coach who famously said: “My desire is to have 100% possession,” after a 5-1 thrashing of Arsenal in Munich during which Thiago Alcântara complete 122 passes.

View image in fullscreen Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca acknowledges the fans before City’s opener against Bournemouth. Photograph: Simon Stacpoole/Offside/Getty Images

Admittedly, Guardiola was speaking out of frustration that day, talking more about not losing the ball at key moments, possession as defence. But these ideas did have a profound mimetic effect in England. During Guardiola’s decade at Manchester City the team that had the least possession in the Premier League would win, on average, only 30%-35% of games, a figure that fell as low as 28% in 2021‑22 but which had begun to pick up in the last two seasons as even City’s own version of Pep‑ball became more mixed and next‑gen.

But this weekend the opposite thing happened. In six of nine games played from Friday to Sunday one team took significantly more possession while failing to win. Liverpool had 60% possession plus 27 shots but still just scrambled a draw and looked, frankly, pretty wild. Manchester United had 71% possession and were well beaten by Hull. Tottenham had 60 % possession and lost 3-0. Nottingham Forest had 56% and lost. Sunderland had 62%, Crystal Palace 58%, and both lost.

There were three exceptions to this, all outliers in their own way. Manchester City had 66% possession and won at home against Bournemouth, but spent 84 minutes looking like they were losing. Brighton had 73% possession and beat an Aston Villa team that had made a collective decision to play with their eyes closed and their legs on the wrong way round.
