Chelsea’s first home fixture is against Luton Town on Thursday in the Carabao Cup with Brighton visiting in the Premier League on Sunday.

Enzo's full-time antics

Chelsea insiders are anticipating an official move from Manchester City for Enzo Fernandez before the summer transfer window closes on September 1, but those inside Stamford Bridge are also entitled to believe they hold the power over this situation.

Fernandez is tied down to a long-term deal, and as shown in Chelsea's Premier League opener away at Fulham, they are happy to keep using him.

They would only sell the Argentine for an enormous sum after spending all summer demanding at least £120million, and they want a replacement lined up. Otherwise, they would be weakening themselves and strengthening a rival.

A video clip on social media appeared to show Fernandez walking away from his Chelsea team-mates and towards the tunnel as they stood in front of the away end following their 3-2 Premier League victory over Fulham.

Chelsea insiders are anticipating an official move from Manchester City for Enzo Fernandez before the summer transfer window closes on September 1

However, Confidential was at Craven Cottage, and in his defence, Fernandez did stand in front of the visiting supporters with everyone else. We then watched as Fernandez gave his shirt to a fan in the home end – we think they were holding a River Plate away shirt if our eyes were not deceiving us, in homage to the team he joined as a six-year-old and represented for 15 years – before exiting.

The BBC’s Match of the Day title credits this season include Fernandez in his Chelsea shirt, shown briefly in between Xavi Simons for Tottenham Hotspur and Erling Haaland for City.

It is almost as if the Beeb are tempting fate after the Argentine's noisy ‘will he, won't he’ summer.

Anything can happen while the summer window remains open and City boss Enzo Maresca made a point of using Marc Guehi in midfield next to Elliot Anderson in their 2-1 comeback win over Bournemouth. Anderson left the field injured in the second half.

Neto asking price puts off Saudi bids

Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal turned their attention to Arsenal’s Gabriel Martinelli after learning that Chelsea valued Pedro Neto at close to £100million.

The Blues slapped that valuation on Neto after noting the asking prices for other wingers in this window and because they appreciate him highly internally.

However, Al Hilal are now getting closer to an agreement for Martinelli instead worth between £50-55million, with Neto relegated to a back-up option.

Neto got an earful from Chelsea captain Reece James during their 3-2 win at Fulham for not tracking back after he replaced Malo Gusto as a right wing-back.

Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal turned their attention to Arsenal’s Gabriel Martinelli (right) after learning that Chelsea valued Pedro Neto (left) at close to £100million

Josh steps in and steps up

The Chelsea predicted lineup in Fulham's matchday programme had Wesley Fofana starting in the visitors’ defence despite being suspended for this clash.

In Fofana’s place, Josh Acheampong impressed, though the 20-year-old academy graduate's situation remains one to watch between now and the end of the window. As revealed by Daily Mail Sport last week, Chelsea have been considering whether to keep him where he is or sanction a loan.

They have long maintained that they do not want to sell him permanently. But performances like the one he put in at Fulham may only tell a few suitors that he is ready for more regular game time.

Sports.title: Man United COMPLETE £70m signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton - as Michael Carrick looks to bolster midfield after Hull horror show on Premier League opening day
Sports.content:
Man United COMPLETE £70m signing of Carlos Baleba from Brighton - as Michael Carrick looks to bolster midfield after Hull horror show on Premier League opening day

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Manchester United have announced the signing of Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba in a £70million deal.

Baleba has signed a five-year-contract at Old Trafford with the option to extend it by 12 months after agreeing personal terms and passing a medical.

United will pay an initial £65m and up to £5m more in add-ons to Brighton who have included a sell-on clause as part of the deal.

The 22-year-old Cameroon international, who is currently sidelined with an ankle injury, becomes United's third midfield signing of the summer after the club spent a total of £85m on Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

Baleba, who has been linked with United for more than a year, said: 'It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

'I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

Carlos Baleba has completed a £70million transfer to Manchester United from Brighton

The 22-year-old has signed a five-year deal at Old Trafford, with the option for an extra year

'The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together.'

United's director of football Jason Wilcox is delighted to complete the club's midfield rebuild after Casemiro left as a free agent and Manuel Ugarte was ruled out for much of this season with a knee ligament injury.

'Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further,' said Wilcox. 'He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

'We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.

'Carlos' determination to join Manchester United and his confidence that we will achieve our shared ambitions mean that he is the perfect signing as we continue to build a dynamic and entertaining team ready to compete across multiple competitions.'

Fans will be relieved to see United get the deal over the line, particularly after their woeful start to the season at Hull City on Saturday.

First-half goals from Semi Ajayi and Nobel Mendy, both coming from set-pieces, left the Mancunians in the dust.

United's midfield of Santos and Tielemans with Fernandes ahead of them, lacked the dynamism that Baleba should hopefully aid with once he's fit.

Sports.title: What's next for Ollie Watkins and Aston Villa: TOM COLLOMOSSE reveals last week's summit with Unai Emery, why he could still sign new contract and Villa's targets to replace star striker if he goes to Saudi
Sports.content:
What's next for Ollie Watkins and Aston Villa: TOM COLLOMOSSE reveals last week's summit with Unai Emery, why he could still sign new contract and Villa's targets to replace star striker if he goes to Saudi

Unlock more from Tom Collomosse inside the Villa camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Ollie Watkins’ absence from the Aston Villa team for the opening-day thrashing at Brighton is the latest chapter in a story that started 18 months ago.

Manager Unai Emery was so enraged by his star striker's omission from the matchday squad on the south coast amid rumours of a move to Saudi Pro League side Al Hilal that he could only reply 'silence' when asked what had caused it, adding: 'I think you can call him, call his agent and he can respond.'

The England forward spoke to his team-mates on Monday to explain his side of the story and was expected to return to some training this week. The stance remains the same: Villa are willing to sell Watkins to the Saudis, but only if their current valuation of at least £50million is matched.

That may shift in the days ahead, with Villa seeking reinforcements in defence, out wide and at centre-forward. Though this row might have been handled differently by both sides, it has not come from a clear blue sky.

Daily Mail Sport looks at how we got here and what might happen next.

Where it all began

At some point last week, Watkins had a discussion with Unai Emery. The Villa boss left those talks believing Watkins wanted to move to Al Hilal and was prepared to go to significant lengths to ensure the deal went through.

Unai Emery was in no mood to protect Ollie Watkins when his star striker was not available for the opening day at Brighton

Al Hilal, whose squad includes former Wolves captain Ruben Neves (furthest right) and Chelsea centre back Kalidou Koulibaly (second right) need to match Villa's £50m valuation

Watkins did not train last week as he waited for Villa to accept a bid. Al Hilal did not make the required offer and once he understood Watkins would not be involved in the preparation work, Emery did not consider him for last Sunday’s match at Brighton.

Without the injured Tammy Abraham and Brian Madjo, strikerless Villa were hammered 4-0 and Emery did nothing in his media appearances to protect Watkins. Sure enough, the 30-year-old was targeted mercilessly by supporters online.

To understand why this happened, we must rewind to a sliding doors moment for Villa and Watkins – Boxing Day 2024. In the previous three league games, Emery had decided to pick Jhon Duran, the chaotic but brilliant Colombian, ahead of Watkins, and Duran had scored in all three.

Heading into the next match at Newcastle, it looked as though Duran had become Villa’s undisputed No1 striker and the club started to make contingency plans for January. They knew Arsenal were chasing a forward and had an interest in Watkins, a boyhood Gunners fan.

Then Duran was given a straight red card at Newcastle and when he completed his suspension, Emery did not feel his form or attitude merited a return to the team. Al Nassr arrived with a £70million offer for Duran and Villa decided to cut their losses on a player who was hugely difficult to manage.

Villa were unwilling to sell both forwards in the same window and Watkins was denied his dream move to Arsenal, whose offers never approached Villa’s £65million valuation. The forward was disappointed but at the end of the window, Emery said: ‘Now we need him, like he needed Aston Villa.’

As far as the Spaniard is concerned, the same applies now. Emery has already lost Youri Tielemans, Morgan Rogers, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa this summer and wants a few senior men to stick with him to build the new era, which includes another Champions League campaign this season.

Usually, Emery does not stand in a player’s way if he wants to depart but this one feels more personal.

Aston Villa have already lost the likes of Youri Tielemans (left) and Morgan Rogers (right) this summer and Watkins (centre) may be next

Jhon Duran was primed to be Villa's No1 striker 18 months ago before a red card at Newcastle

Contrasting positions

Watkins is easily the top client at Two Touch, the agency run by former Arsenal youngster Paolo Vernazza which represents an extensive list of players including Watkins’ Villa team-mate Matty Cash and Crystal Palace midfielder Will Hughes.

If Watkins were to move to Al Hilal, it would likely be one of Two Touch’s biggest deals and it is clear Villa are unhappy with how Vernazza has handled it. Vernazza may yet push this one through but were he to have his time again, he might make a different plan. Daily Mail Sport has attempted to contact Vernazza since Sunday but he has yet to respond.

Watkins is thought to earn a little more than £100,000 a week at Villa yet the salary proposed by Al Hilal is thought to be substantially more. Watkins has been Villa’s leading scorer in every season since he joined from Brentford in 2020 and is their all-time top Premier League marksman.

He has also seen Ezri Konsa, who is two years younger, allowed to join Arsenal for roughly the same sum Villa want from Al Hilal. Watkins turns 31 in December and if he believed Villa’s price was too high for a player his age, you could understand it. Not surprisingly, Villa see it differently.

Since Emery took charge in 2022, Watkins has developed into one of the best strikers in Europe, thanks also to Emery’s willingness to back him. Duran had to score five times after coming off the bench before he was given a run in the side. Donyell Malen was sold to Roma last January because Emery backed Watkins over the Dutchman, who has since scored 18 times in 21 games for the Serie A club.

Even when Watkins scored only once before December last season, and only once more between January 4 and March 11, Emery kept faith – and was rewarded when his main man hit 12 in 13 games at the end of the season to force his way into England’s World Cup squad.

Emery has lost four key players this summer and with two forwards injured, he felt he really needed Watkins at Brighton. No wonder he was ticking before the pre-match interviews. With Emery, the less he says, often the angrier he is.

He looked a man on the edge at the Amex Stadium, where he argued with the fourth official far more than usual, grew irritable with the opposing bench and stalked down the tunnel at full time without approaching Albion boss Fabian Hurzeler for a handshake. Emery and Hurzeler are certainly not best friends, but the reaction was still telling.

Emery looked a man on the edge at the Amex Stadium, where he argued with the fourth official far more than usual and grew irritable with the opposing bench

Watkins struck 12 goals in the final 13 games of last season to force his way into England's squad for the World Cup, where he scored in the warm-up against Costa Rica

Is there a way back?

A year ago, it looked as though Emiliano Martinez had played his final game for Villa. Desperate to move to Manchester United or Atletico Madrid, Martinez was not included in the Villa side for the home defeat by Crystal Palace – a display just as bad as the Brighton one.

Martinez is still at Villa today, still trying to get out, though he knuckled down last season and helped the club win the Europa League. So it would be foolish to write off Watkins’ Villa career just yet.

The Saudi Pro League’s top clubs can also be ruthless. If they decide a target is no longer worth pursuing, they will move on. Right now, that is the nightmare scenario for Watkins.

Yet the best outcome for all parties is probably to agree a deal. Watkins would have a huge job winning over Villa fans again. If he moves, he will have his new chapter and Villa will be able to pursue his replacement.

If Watkins stays Villa will give him a new deal, but that risks a loveless marriage. Despite the late goal rush, there were signs last season that Watkins was in decline. Do player or club really want to be tied to one another for the next two or three seasons?

There have already been informal talks behind the scenes regarding Nicolas Jackson and Emery is keen on the Chelsea striker, who he coached at Villarreal. In midfield, they hope Leon Goretzka will arrive while there have been discussions for Club Brugge centre-back Joel Ordonez, even though he is injured.

There have already been informal talks behind the scenes regarding Nicolas Jackson and Emery is keen on the Chelsea striker, who he coached at Villarreal

There have been discussions for Club Brugge centre-back Joel Ordonez (right), even though he is injured. Either way, Villa need Watkins’ future sorted before they host Arsenal on Monday

Either way, Villa need Watkins’ future sorted before they take on Arsenal at Villa Park on Monday.

With both Abraham and Madjo still struggling, one of Villa’s best-ever forwards risks being booed by some of his own fans in their first home game of the season, against the team he supported.

If nothing else, that prospect should focus a few minds.

Sports.title: Chelsea write to fans to urge them to stop singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' after chant was aired against at Fulham
Sports.content:
Chelsea write to fans to urge them to stop singing 'f*** the Pope and the IRA' after chant was aired against at Fulham

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Chelsea are to write to fans – and warn them of potential bans – after a section of the club’s support launched into a sectarian chant at their 3-2 win at Fulham.

During the west London derby a chorus of the ‘Flute for 50 pence song’ was clearly audible from the away section at Craven Cottage.

The song includes the line ‘F*** the Pope and the IRA’ and its airing would appear to reflect the long-standing relationship between elements of the club’s support and that of Glasgow Rangers.

Chelsea officials are aware of the chant, which is thought to have seen a resurgence in recent times, and have decided to act.

Daily Mail Sport understands they will trace those who bought tickets for the fixture, and email them to ask them to avoid any repeat. It is likely to be made clear that anyone found doing so will face a ban from attending matches.

The Football Association is thought to be aware of the situation.

Sports.title: Why Tottenham's new £85m signing wants to be called Savio not Savinho... as boss Roberto De Zerbi tells new man the area he must improve
Sports.content:
Why Tottenham's new £85m signing wants to be called Savio not Savinho... as boss Roberto De Zerbi tells new man the area he must improve

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Roberto De Zerbi hailed Savinho among the world's best one-on-one dribblers and told Tottenham's new signing it was now time to add goals to his game.

Spurs will pay Manchester City up to £85million for the Brazil international who wants to be known from this point forward as Savio.

The 22-year-old was named by his father in tribute to Savio, a Brazil winger who played for Flamengo and Real Madrid at the turn of the century.

He became known as Savinho, informally Little Savio, a common derivative in Latin America football, during a meteoric rise through Brazil's youth ranks.

The precise name on his No.17 shirt is the least of De Zerbi's problems after losing 3-0 at Brentford on Saturday.

De Zerbi is simply delighted to sign a player he tried to sign from Troyes when he was in charge at Brighton and who Spurs have been actively chasing for more than a year.

'We need players capable to win one-on-ones, to create something, create chances to score,' said De Zerbi. 'In terms of the one-on-one he's one of the best. He can play right or left side. He's a big player for us, a big signing.'

Savio is still young, but his progress has stalled at City where he has scored two Premier League goals in two years since signing from City Group sister club Troyes after scoring 11 goals in 41 games during a season on loan at Girona in Spain.

Roberto De Zerbi has hailed new £85million signing Savinho after his arrival from Man City

The Brazilian wants to be known as 'Savio' after completing his move to the North Londoners

'To be complete he has to score,' said De Zerbi. 'If you analyse the best wingers in the world, many of them score 10-15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe he has to change habits because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-vs-one dribbling and also to score.

'Because we have to increase the number of chances to score and the number of goals. You become a top team scoring more goals.'

As for the delay in signing Savio, De Zerbi added: 'I am not patient. We started the negotiations for Savio three days or a week after the Everton game [in May] and for many reasons he arrived in the last week of August.

'If you want the highest quality level of players, it's right to wait. We always have a Plan B or Plan C, but players are not like smartphones. They're different so they come with different personalities, experiences, characteristics, potential.'

Spurs are also close to signing City's Omar Marmoush, initially on loan with an obligation to buy next year for £50m and working on a deal for Cody Gakpo from Liverpool ahead of the transfer deadline on Monday.

Spurs boss De Zerbi has told the Brazilian he needs to improve his goalscoring numbers

Signing players from successful clubs is integral to De Zerbi's bid to impose a winning mentality on his team, and he will insist they approach Tuesday's Carabao Cup second round tie at home against Charlton of the Championship like a Premier League fixture.

'We have to play well and get used to winning matches and matches,' said De Zerbi. 'Not one match, but one, two, three and four matches. We have to change the mood and we can. The environment has to change the players have to change this mentality.'

Savio is eligible to play against Charlton. Dominic Solanke is set to start with new captain Micky van de Ven and new vice-captain Pedro Porro back on the bench. James Maddison will not be involved after picking up a minor shoulder injury against Brentford.

Sports.title: Revealed: Brydon Carse WAS arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly during nightclub visit with Ben Stokes - with police now RE-OPENING investigation into England bowler
Sports.content:
Revealed: Brydon Carse WAS arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly during nightclub visit with Ben Stokes - with police now RE-OPENING investigation into England bowler

Brydon Carse was briefly arrested on suspicion of being ‘drunk and disorderly’ in Derby on Saturday night, before being de-arrested, it has emerged.

Carse was dropped earlier today from England’s squad for Thursday’s second Test against Pakistan at Lord’s while the Cricket Regulator investigates the events that led to police handcuffing him outside a nightclub.

He was then de-arrested - meaning the arrest was cancelled before he was taken into custody. But Daily Mail Sport understands the matter is now back in the hands of the police, who are looking into the precise sequence of events.

A statement by Derbyshire police read: ‘A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in Derby city centre on Saturday night. However the man was de-arrested shortly afterwards having agreed to leave the area.’

Brydon Carse was handcuffed by police outside the nightclub in Derby

Ben Stokes (in background) was also in attendance after Durham's big win over Derbyshire

Carse has been replaced in the 16-man squad by Hampshire fast bowler Sonny Baker

It is understood the man in question is 31-year-old Carse, who has been replaced in the 16-man squad by Hampshire fast bowler Sonny Baker.

A social-media video showed the moment Carse was handcuffed, with four policemen in attendance, and Durham team-mates Ben Stokes and Matthew Potts both featuring briefly on camera.

And while Carse, who has not played a Test since last winter's Ashes, was not on England duty, he has an ECB central contract.

After a year in which Harry Brook, Ben Duckett and Stokes have been involved in separate alcohol-related incidents, the sight of another England cricketer making headlines for the wrong reasons has not gone down well at Lord’s.

An ECB statement said: ‘Brydon Carse will no longer be available for selection for the Second Men’s Rothesay Test Match while this investigation is ongoing and the full facts are obtained.’

The Cricket Regulator has at is disposal a range of options, including no further action, caution or bringing a charge for a breach of the regulations – among them, bringing the game into disrepute.

Sports.title: Man Utd announce Carlos Baleba transfer in £70m deal as next signing becomes clear
Sports.content:
Man Utd announce Carlos Baleba transfer in £70m deal as next signing becomes clear

Carlos Baleba has signed a five-year contract with Manchester United, who've finally completed their midfield rebuild with just one week to go before the summer transfer window slams shut

View 2 Images Carlos Baleba has officially joined Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have announced the signing of Carlos Baleba in a deal worth up to £70million. Baleba, 22, has put pen to paper on a five-year contract at Old Trafford, with the option of the further 12 months, and leaves Brighton after three impressive seasons.

‌



United will pay an initial £65m plus a potential £5m in add-ons. Brighton have also negotiated a sell-on clause for the midfielder they bought from French side Lille in 2023.

‌



Baleba becomes the Red Devils' third midfield signing of the summer, joining Andrey Santos (£50m) and Youri Tielemans (£35m). United will now focus on other areas during the final week of the transfer window, with left-back a priority.

‌



Contact has been made for Barcelona's Alejandro Balde, who was left out of their squad to face Elche on Sunday. A forward is also on United's shopping list, but that may depend on the future of Joshua Zirkzee.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Having completed his medical over the weekend, Baleba said: "It is an incredible feeling to join the club of my dreams. Playing at Old Trafford is always special but the opportunity to do so as a Manchester United player will be a real honour.

"I cannot wait to work with Michael Carrick; his experience and knowledge of the game make him the perfect coach to help me to reach the highest level.

"The ambition of everyone at the club is extremely clear, the future is hugely exciting, and I am determined to play my part in delivering the success that we are capable of together."

‌



United's director of football, Jason Wilcox, added: "Carlos is an elite midfielder with immense potential to develop further. He brings a unique combination of qualities that will really complement our squad.

"We are delighted to further strengthen our midfield with the addition of another established senior international with a proven track record of performing in the Premier League.

"Carlos' determination to join Manchester United and his confidence that we will achieve our shared ambitions mean that he is the perfect signing as we continue to build a dynamic and entertaining team ready to compete across multiple competitions."

‌



Who should Manchester United sign next? Let us know your pick in the comments section.

View 2 Images Manchester United wanted to sign Carlos Baleba a year ago (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Baleba isn't expected to make his debut until next month, with the Cameroon international nursing an ankle ligament injury which ruled him out of Brighton's first two games. United host Ipswich this Sunday looking for their first point of the season, as Michael Carrick's side suffered an abject 2-0 defeat away to Hull in their opening Premier League game.

‌



Their need for a player like Baleba was no more evident than against Hull, as they sorely lacked a midfielder capable of covering ground and winning back possession. United did the groundwork on the 22-year-old last summer when Brighton quoted United £100m for his services.

But the club's patience has paid off, signing him for a considerably lower fee this time around. His arrival takes United's spending to £155m, with their other newcomer, goalkeeper Karl Darlow, joining on a free after his contract with Leeds expired.

Sports.title: Ashley Cole leaves England U21 set-up after five years and sets sight on new role
Sports.content:
Ashley Cole leaves England U21 set-up after five years and sets sight on new role

The Football Association have confirmed that former Arsenal and England defender Ashley Cole has left his position with the national team's Under-21s

View 2 Images Ashley Cole is looking for a club role after leaving the England U21s (Image: Nathan Stirk/Getty Images)

Ashley Cole has left his role with England under-21s after five years as a coach.

‌



Former England defender Cole was part of under-21s boss Lee Carsley’s coaching staff which won back-to-back European titles. Cole retired from his playing career in 2019 and moved into coaching and it is believed he wants to carry on at club level.

‌



Carsley said Cole had a “positive, inspirational impact on his players” and added: “I want to pay tribute to Ashley who played a major part in our two Euro wins and also had a key role in the current campaign with his tactical and technical knowledge.

‌



“I am certain he will have even more success in his coaching career whatever the future holds.”

Cole worked under Frank Lampard at Derby, had a spell at Chelsea ’s academy and then was assistant manager at Everton and Birmingham.

‌



The ex-Arsenal and Chelsea left back is one of England’s all-time great defenders and he had a recent spell as head coach of Serie B club Cesena in March after not getting a chance in his own right in English football.

But Cole, who won 107 caps and three Premier League titles and a European Cup during his glorious playing career, left Cesena in June, citing a “change in the club's strategy.”

Cole took to social media to explain his departure, writing: “As my tenure at Cesena FC concludes today, I want to thank the players and staff for their hard work and commitment over the last few months.

“I was proud to bring my experience to such a passionate club, and I’ve truly enjoyed working with the squad to introduce a new identity and prepare for the season ahead.

“Following recent discussions with the Sporting Director regarding a change in the club’s strategy, I have decided that it is best for me to move on.

“I leave with great respect for all the people there, as well as the fans, and look forward to my next challenge.”

Sports.title: Billy Boston broke the mould - he was a true pioneer of rugby league and beyond
Sports.content:
Billy Boston broke the mould - he was a true pioneer of rugby league and beyond

Billy Boston will leave behind a legacy that will endure for generations to come - while the word 'legend' felt like an understatement when it came to the try-scoring phenomenon

View 3 Images The great Billy Boston has died aged 92 (Image: Photo by Aaron Chown - WPA Pool / Getty Images)

Sir Billy Boston broke the mould. A pioneer of his chosen sport, one which he graced with such distinction and class.

‌



Boston also broke through tackles and broke down barriers in equal measure. From lighting up Wembley to crushing the great Australians at Sydney Cricket Ground, Boston went on to become a blur of speed, skill and strength few could - or ever will - be able to match.

‌



He scored an astonishing 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan, and helped Great Britain win the 1960 World Cup, scoring in the final defeat of the Aussies.

‌



But his glorious achievements on the pitch were matched off it as well. Boston was born in Cardiff in 1934 and had 10 siblings.

He wanted to represent Cardiff at Rugby Union, but when his hometown club rejected him he joined Wigan as a teenager. He became the first black player to tour Down Under with Great Britain.

Sir Billy Boston dies as tributes pour in for rugby legend and World Cup winner READ MORE :

‌



He was one of the first players to be inducted into the Rugby League 'Hall of Fame', the first to be inducted into the Welsh one and is cast in bronze in both Wigan and Cardiff.

And last but by no means least, in 2025 Boston became the first and only rugby league player to be knighted.

3 View 3 Images Boston dodges a tackle during his Wigan days (Image: Alamy Stock Photo) 3 View 3 Images Boston was an icon of the sport (Image: ANL/Shutterstock)

‌



He unified what was, at the time of his peak, a tribal and divided Rugby League community. To such an extent that his popularity in the game even stretched to St Helens, the long-time bitter rivals of his beloved Wigan.

In a post-war Britain, Boston was the trailblazing black athlete who brought people together in a country adjusting to a more diverse way of life.

The word 'legend' can be bandied about too often. But when it came to Boston, it felt like an understatement. That's how good he was. Arguably the greatest player Britain has ever had.

Article continues below

A giant on the wing - and a sporting icon of the swinging Sixties, leading the way for all those greats who went on to switch codes after he did.

Rivals spoke of Boston's hand off feeling like 'being hit in the face with a shovel'. Which feels ironic - because Boston dug himself a reputation for having set the kind of example that will endure for generations to come.

Gone but never forgotten - Boston was truly one of a kind.

Sports.title: Nicky Henderson announces decision on Constitution Hill Windsor appearance
Sports.content:
Nicky Henderson announces decision on Constitution Hill Windsor appearance

The Champion Hurdle winner was entered for a first start on the Flat on Turf on Saturday but the lack of rain has been troubling trainer Nicky Henderson

View 2 Images Constitution Hill (centre): set to return to Kempton (Image: PA)

Nicky Henderson has made an early call on whether Constitution Hill will return to Flat action on Saturday.

‌



The winner of the 2023 Champion Hurdle at the Cheltenham Festival switched codes after a sequence of three falls in four races, making his Flat debut in February when he recorded a stunning win at Southwell, scoring by seven lengths before a record crowd for the Nottinghamshire track.

‌



Then he won another novice stakes at Kempton in March and is ready to resume his new career following a short break. His name features among 19 entries for the Listed Weatherbys August Stakes at Windsor on Saturday.

‌



Arc-winning trainer announces stable closure with business set to go into liquidation READ MORE :

Jockey banned from riding for six months after police called to changing room punch-up READ MORE :

Henderson made it clear it would have to rain for him to take his chance yet 24 hours after making the entry he has made his mind up.

In a post on his X account, he said: "We all very much appreciate all the interest let alone the speculation as to Constitution Hill’s next race, but, between Michael & I and all the team, we have decided, in order to avoid further uncertainty and any possibility of a late withdrawal, to wait for the September Stakes at Kempton a week on Saturday, as opposed to Windsor this weekend.

‌



View 2 Images Nicky Henderson with Constitution Hill at Kempton (Image: Getty Images)

"There are, in fact, several factors apart from the ground that have influenced our decision. Having spoken to jockeys who rode at Windsor last night, and Charlie Rees (Clerk of the Course), who I know is doing everything to combat this dry spell, the chances of the ground being suitable on Saturday are highly unlikely.

"Kempton is obviously going to be a highly competitive Group 3, but we have got to start somewhere in order to find out where he belongs and establish an autumn campaign.

Article continues below

"We are hoping that one of the two jockeys who know him [Oisin Murphy and Ryan Moore] could be available for the September Stakes, which they are unlikely to be this weekend. We all think he is in excellent shape and although he will undoubtedly benefit from this run he is ready to do himself justice."

Sports.title: Man Utd face major Alejandro Balde transfer issue as they search for Lewis Hall alternative
Sports.content:
Man Utd face major Alejandro Balde transfer issue as they search for Lewis Hall alternative

Manchester United want to add a left-back to their squad before the summer transfer window closes for business on September 1 and have identified Alejandro Balde as a target

View 2 Images Alejandro Balde is available from Barcelona (Image: Jose Breton/Getty Images)

Manchester United have been offered the chance to sign Barcelona left-back Alejandro Balde, but are reportedly unwilling to pay the asking price.

‌



United remain in the hunt to sign a left-back before the summer transfer window closes on September 1. Their initial number one target Lewis Hall now appears to be out of reach, with Newcastle unwilling to discuss a deal after selling a handful of other stars.

‌



That has led United to move onto other options, with manager Michael Carrick still keen to bring in competition for Luke Shaw, who is in his 13th season at the club and has historically suffered with injuries. United's dreadful performance in a 2-0 defeat by newly-promoted Hull on Saturday has further underlined the need for new arrivals.

‌



Balde was left out of the Barcelona squad for their 5-0 thrashing of Elche on Sunday and the 22-year-old could soon be on the move. “I spoke with Balde and told him that, in my opinion, he is not 100 per cent ready," manager Hansi Flick said. "That he should sort out his thoughts, and then we will discuss it.”

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



The Athletic reports that, while Barca are open to selling, they value Balde, who has nearly two years left on his contract, at €45million (£38.5m). That is too much for United, who would instead look for an initial loan deal.

Balde came through the Barcelona academy and has made 168 appearances since making his debut in 2021. He is understood to want assurances of game time if he is to stay at the club for the 2026/27 campaign.

United's hopes of finding a left-back could rely on Jorge Mendes, who represents both Balde and another target, Jorge Salinas. The 19-year-old Racing Santander defender has a release clause of just €16m (£13.6m) in his contract, but is also in talks with Atletico Madrid.

‌



View 2 Images Jorge Salinas is another possible target for Manchester United (Image: Cesar Ortiz Gonzalez/NurPhoto via Getty Images)

As well as Shaw, United have other options in the form of Patrick Dorgu, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui. However, Dorgu has been deployed on the left wing by Carrick, while Dalot and Mazraoui are more comfortable at right-back. Academy graduate Harry Amass has been made available for another loan spell away from the club.

Left-back is the last remaining piece of the puzzle for United this summer after they struck an agreement to sign Carlos Baleba from Brighton for a fee which could reach £70m. The Cameroon international is set to be announced after undergoing a medical over the weekend and will join Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in a new-look midfield.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel sends immediate message to Michael Carrick after shock Man Utd loss
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel sends immediate message to Michael Carrick after shock Man Utd loss

JJ Gabriel has progressed further up the ranks at Manchester United

View 3 Images JJ Gabriel celebrates during his competitive debut for Manchester United U21s (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

JJ Gabriel has given Michael Carrick a timely reminder of his quality as the Manchester United youngster presses his case for a Premier League appearance.

‌



Following Saturday's abject defeat at Hull City, Carrick saw a much more heartening performance on Monday night as the under-21s thrashed Ipswich Town 5-0 at Leigh's Progress with Unity Stadium. The forward, still only 15, stole the show with a goal and two assists on his competitive debut for the U21s, despite being dwarfed by several Ipswich players.

‌



If United's stuttering start to the season continues, Carrick may be tempted to draft him into the first-team squad earlier than expected. The United boss has already seen enough to invite him to train with the team last season and then take him on the recent pre-season tour.

‌



As he was 14 when last season began, he was unable to play for the first team in the Premier League. There are now no such restrictions and it would be a surprise if he doesn't figure for the first team at some stage this season.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Speaking about the youngster in March, Carrick said: "He is not allowed [to be part of a first-team squad on a matchday]. He's too young.

‌



Paul Scholes lashes out at Bruno Fernandes after Man Utd skipper slated team-mates READ MORE :

Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher make Premier League predictions with shock relegation candidate READ MORE :

"JJ's doing really well. We've got some really good players in the academy and we try and get the younger players up [with the main group] as much as we can.

"We're always trying to give them that exposure. JJ is a big talent, it is pretty obvious and he has had a good season for U18s. We think an awful lot of him.

View 3 Images Gabriel held his own against much bigger players (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



"But patience is important in managing everything that comes with that and developing him and picking the right moment to step up, to leave them in a certain place. He's trained well and it is good to have young players up."

The chances of Gabriel, who turns 16 in October, graduating to the first team could rest on the transfer business United get done over the final week of the transfer window.

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has plenty to ponder after United's defeat at Hull (Image: Getty Images)

‌



After a bright start to the summer, with Youri Tielemans among the arrivals, progress stalled somewhat, leaving fans fearful that the momentum made under Carrick over the second half of last season is being lost.

There has at least been progress in recent days, with long-time target Carlos Baleba on his way from Brighton for £70million. He could be followed to Old Trafford by another Seagulls player in left-back Ferdi Kadioglu. There are also calls for United to add to their attacking options.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
