World.title: US dollar exchange rate slightly falls against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight decline on Tuesday in both Baghdad, the capital of Iraq, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate slightly declined in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,542.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,543.5 Iraqi dinars on Tuesday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,547.5 Iraqi dinars and 1,537.5 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate dropped, fluctuating between 1,544.5 and 1,543.5 Iraqi dinars.

The Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) said in February 2023 that it has begun using the new US dollar exchange rate of 1,300 dinars to every US dollar.

The previous official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars to one US dollar, which was being exchanged in the parallel market at a rate of 1,550 dinars.

While the official exchange rate was 1,450 dinars per dollar in January 2023, the US currency was being exchanged at 1,610 dinars during the same month in the parallel market in Iraq. This variation indicated a difference of over 10 percent in the exchange rates.

World.title: Iraq, Germany discuss international coalition withdrawal
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and Commander of German Forces Deployed Abroad, Gunter Schneider, met on Monday in Baghdad to organize the US-led international coalition forces’ imminent withdrawal from Iraq.

The meeting addressed strategies to strengthen bilateral relations between Iraq and Germany in the military and security fields through initiatives aiming to improve the performance of the Iraqi armed forces, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister stressed the need to develop broader partnerships with the international coalition’s member countries. He praised Germany for aiding Iraq in its battle against terrorism, notably during the confrontation with ISIS.

Al-Zaidi said earlier that the military mission of the international coalition will expire on September 30, 2026, and that the decision is final and irreversible.

The prime minister underscored that October 1 will bring in a new period of total Iraqi independence and full territorial sovereignty, with no foreign military presence.

Iraq’s future interactions with the international coalition’s member states will focus on direct security, economic, and specialized training cooperation based on mutual respect.

The international coalition was first formed in 2014 to combat the emergence of the terrorist group ISIS.

After Iraq declared military victory over ISIS in 2017, international coalition forces continued to provide advice and training services at Baghdad’s request.

The official withdrawal of the international coalition follows a bilateral arrangement agreed upon by Baghdad and Washington.

World.title: Nasiriyah International Airport reaches 68% completion, targets early 2027 opening
World.content:
Nasiriyah (IraqiNews.com) — Construction work on the Nasiriyah International Airport project in Dhi Qar Governorate has reached a 68% overall completion rate, according to statements made on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, by Captain Ihab Saad, Director General of the General Company for Airports Management and Air Navigation Services.

Saad characterized the construction momentum as continuous and accelerating, confirming that the facility is projected for official delivery in early 2027, provided current construction schedules proceed without unforeseen disruptions.

Technical Milestones & Equipment Inspection

Current Progress: Civil and structural engineering works stand at 68% completion.

Ground Handling Systems: Progress rates are set to increase significantly upon the delivery and installation of new ground handling and airfield equipment batches.

Factory Acceptance Testing in China: A specialized technical committee is traveling to China to conduct rigorous factory acceptance tests on navigational, baggage, and ground operations equipment prior to on-site installation.

Contractual Adjustments: Project authorities have resolved primary operational bottlenecks and are finalizing a new contract appendix to formally settle remaining technical and logistical requirements.

The foundation stone for Nasiriyah International Airport was laid in June 2021 to serve as a major commercial and logistics hub for southern Iraq:

International Contractors: In mid-July 2024, the Ministry of Transport finalized a consultancy and design contract appendix with Turkish firm Kiklop Design Hertz Insaat, alongside an amended engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contract with China State Construction Engineering Corporation (CSCEC).

Delivery Schedule Evolution: Following earlier timeline revisions from late 2025 into early 2026, project management has established early 2027 as the targeted commissioning window to accommodate factory testing, equipment integration, and final aviation certification.

Upon completion, Nasiriyah International Airport will serve as a critical gateway for passenger transit, business investment, and cultural tourism in Dhi Qar, providing direct international connectivity to the ancient city of Ur, the Mesopotamian Marshes (Ahwar), and surrounding southern industrial zones.

World.title: Iraq continues to be South Korea’s fourth-largest oil supplier
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq was the fourth largest crude oil supplier to South Korea in the first half of 2026, accounting for 7.4 percent of the country’s total oil imports.

According to the Korea Petroleum Association (KPA) and the Korea National Oil Corporation, South Korea imported 467.12 million barrels of crude oil in the first half of the year, an eight percent decline compared to the same period in 2025.

However, the value of the country’s oil imports increased by 8.1 percent to $41.36 billion as global oil prices surged, local news outlet Shafaq News reported.

Saudi Arabia was the largest supplier of oil to South Korea, making up 30.5 percent of the country’s total oil imports. The United States followed with over 20 percent of South Korea’s crude oil imports.

Oil supplies from the United Arab Emirates accounted for 15.1 percent of South Korea’s oil imports.

The figures indicate a notable shift in South Korea’s oil supplies, with Middle Eastern oil falling from 68.7 percent to 62.3 percent throughout the time. This shift is basically due to the effects of the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which caused interruptions in oil supplies worldwide.

Iraq’s average oil shipments to South Korea totaled 113.7 million barrels in 2025, which is an average of 311,500 barrels per day. This represents a 12 percent increase compared to 2024.

World.title: Iraq U20 Draws 0-0 with Iran to Wrap Up Thailand Training Camp
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraq Under-20 national football team played to a 0–0 draw against Iran on Tuesday, August 25, 2026, in Bangkok, concluding their final overseas preparatory camp ahead of the upcoming AFC U20 Asian Cup qualifiers.

The friendly encounter was attended by Iraq Football Association (IFA) Executive Board members Khalaf Jalal, who heads the youth national team delegation, and Abdul Razzaq Akram Al-Shalah.

Iraq completes its preparatory training camp in Thailand with an unbeaten 3-match run:

Match 1: Iraq 1 – 0 Kuwait

Match 2: Iraq 2 – 1 Indonesia

Match 3: Iraq 0 – 0 Iran

The scoreless draw against Iran provided the coaching staff with a high-intensity defensive and tactical test against one of the continent’s perennial youth powerhouses, following back-to-back victories against Kuwait and Indonesia earlier in the camp.

Following the conclusion of the Bangkok camp, the Iraqi youth squad will relocate to the host city of Chonburi, Thailand, to begin their official qualification campaign.

Iraq has been drawn into Group F, competing against:

Thailand(Host nation)

United Arab Emirates

Turkmenistan

The group winners, alongside the best-ranked runners-up across all qualification groups, will secure direct berths to the final tournament of the AFC U20 Asian Cup.

World.title: U.S. prepares to return diplomats to Iraq and Middle East
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The United States is preparing to return evacuated foreign service personnel to several diplomatic missions across the Middle East, according to an internal U.S. State Department document and confirmations from three U.S. officials reported by The New York Times on Tuesday, August 25, 2026.

The decision indicates that Washington does not anticipate a return to full-scale regional hostilities following recent conflict escalations, despite stalled direct talks between Washington and Tehran and renewed threats of economic sanctions.

Phased Staffing Levels by Mission

The State Department’s operational plan outlines specific staffing quotas and regional safety parameters:

Iraq, Kuwait, and Bahrain: Restoring on-site diplomatic staff up to 75% capacity.

UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Lebanon: Restoring on-site personnel up to 85% capacity, with Lebanon receiving some of the earliest returnees.

Israel, Jordan, and Oman: Authorizing a 100% full return of diplomatic personnel.

Dependent Travel Restrictions: Washington will maintain strict restrictions on accompanying family members across Lebanon and all six Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) states, reflecting a calibrated security posture where overall threat levels have declined relative to the peak of the conflict but remain elevated compared to baseline conditions.

The planned return follows progressive emergency evacuations initiated in late February and early March 2026:

Pre-Strike Precautionary Moves: In late February 2026, non-essential personnel and family members at the U.S. mission in Jerusalem were offered voluntary departure immediately preceding joint military operations.

Baghdad Evacuations and Standoff: In early March 2026, the State Department ordered the mandatory drawdown of non-emergency staff across regional posts, including Baghdad, ahead of drone and rocket strikes targeting the U.S. Embassy compound on March 17.

Ceasefire Dynamics: While a 60-day ceasefire expired last week without formal renewal terms finalized, U.S. security assessments determined that resuming partial mission staffing balances operational foreign policy objectives with on-ground personnel safety.

Former U.S. diplomatic and defense officials noted that while redeploying personnel underscores an administrative assessment that active war footing is receding, emergency contingency mechanisms remain in place should regional security dynamics shift.

World.title: Iraq discusses launching direct flights to Austria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The first deputy speaker of the Iraqi parliament, Adnan al-Dulaimi, and the Austrian ambassador to Iraq, Axel Wech, discussed on Tuesday the launch of direct flights between Baghdad and Vienna.

During their meeting in Baghdad, the two sides discussed strategies to develop bilateral relations and activate the meetings of the Iraqi-Austrian Joint Committee within the framework of the Economic and Technical Cooperation Agreement, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Both sides emphasized the need to establish a direct air link between Baghdad and Vienna to improve collaboration in a variety of sectors, notably the economy.

Iraqi and Austrian officials have held high-level discussions, including most recently during the Munich Security Conference, to push for the formal resumption of direct passenger flights between Baghdad and Vienna.

During a meeting with Austrian Interior Minister Gerhard Karner in February, Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein urged Austria to resume direct flights between Baghdad and Vienna.

The Iraqi foreign minister stated that the return of direct flights between Baghdad and Vienna, given the considerable improvement in security in Iraq, will stimulate travel and economic and tourism interchange between the two countries.

The negotiations built on a prior agreement between Iraqi and Austrian aviation officials to help pave the way for European airlines.

Both parties underline that direct flights will boost bilateral trade, reduce travel restrictions, promote tourism, and make mobility easier for foreign investors.

World.title: Iraqi security recovers rare antiquities
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi National Security Service (INSS) arrested an antiquities trafficking network, recovering hundreds of unique artifacts from six different provinces.

The intelligence-guided operations, approved by the local judiciary, targeted black-market dealers and smugglers in Baghdad, Kirkuk, Nineveh, Anbar, Babil, and Wasit.

The INSS said in a statement that the recovered artifacts include five rare ancient statues seized in Baghdad, five historic pottery pieces, an ancient cylinder seal, hundreds of ancient metal and rare gold coins, and numerous ancient manuscripts.

The coordinated operations resulted in the arrest of several alleged antiquities smugglers, according to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The suspects have been transferred to judicial bodies to face criminal charges under Iraq’s antiquities protection laws.

The items seized are being legally processed before being handed over to the National Museum of Iraq for preservation.

This campaign is part of Baghdad’s battle to reclaim its cultural identity.

Iraq’s rich legacy has suffered significant losses, beginning with the looting of approximately 15,000 items from the country’s national museum during the 2003 battle and continuing with widespread illegal excavations and black-market sales carried out by ISIS terrorists after 2014.

Over the previous few years, the government has recovered over 40,000 artifacts from global and domestic criminal markets following internal security operations and international initiatives.

World.title: Did India hit Kirana Hills during Op Sindoor? Ex-CDS Anil Chauhan clears air
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Former Chief of Defence Staff Anil Chauhan on Tuesday said India may have hit Pakistan's Kirana Hills during

last year, but the strike was unintentional.

Speaking at the âVIMARSHâ event on Operation Sindoor and its aftermath at the Vivekanand International Foundation, Chauhan said Indian loitering missions sent to search for radars around Sargodha ran out of fuel and ended up hitting Kirana Hills -- a site associated with Pakistan's nuclear facilities.

"At occasions, it's been asked whether Kirana Hills were hit or not, which is where their (Pakistan's) nuclear facilities are... Before those strikes, we had sent in a lot of loitering missions at Sargodha and Kirana Hills is about 10 kilometers north of Sargodha," Chauhan said.

"So the loitering mission is looking for radars which are in and around Sargodha, and it has a lifetime, which means it will loiter for about 2 hours and once it does not find a target, it comes down and hits somewhere.

It must have come and hit one of those hills. So that could be one of the reasons as to what people asked, because Pakistani media also showed some kind of images in which there was smoke coming out from Kirana Hills," he added.

Chauhan also revealed details of another episode during the operation, saying the Air Chief sought his approval to strike Sargodha after Pakistan requested talks. However the target was changed to Bholari due to bad weather.





"Once the Pakistanis had picked up the phone and said they wanted to talk at about 10 AM. The Air Chief asked me whether he should strike Sargodha, I said, Go ahead. I said, could you please identify two more targets, so one of the targets he identified was Skardu," Chauhan said.

"We gave a yes, but after some time, the weather was bad over it and they had to change over to Bholari," he added.

During his address, Chauhan also stressed that military decisions involve varying levels of risk and must be assessed against the political objectives they are intended to achieve.

"Each option has a certain kind of risk involved in it, and also it will satisfy the political need for which it was to be used. So, itâs an interplay between risk and attainment of political objectives," he said.

Chauhan said the operation remains relevant nearly 15 months after its major active phase ended. He said its assessment should take into account deficiencies identified during the operation, measures taken to address them and the changing nature of warfare.

He added that these factors, along with wider global uncertainties, are creating new challenges for military planners.

World.title: ‘100%’, ‘Energy Drink’, immunity claims: FSSAI flags 6 food firms
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Claims that promise more, sound healthier or make a product appear superior have come under the scanner of the food regulator, with the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (

) flagging misleading claims by six food business operators (FBOs) and directing corrective action.

The cases range from the use of â100%â on coconut oil and âEnergy Drinkâ on a caffeinated beverage to claims around immunity, growth, digestion and nutrition in baby food, as well as health and nutrient-comparison claims.

Mondelez India Foods Pvt Ltd was flagged over misleading health and nutrient comparative claims. It subsequently withdrew the claims and s from e-commerce platforms.

Sapiens Labs was flagged over a misleading claim and, after submitting its response, withdrew the claim and s.

Vichi Agro Products Pvt Ltd, along with the concerned packer, was flagged over a misleading trade name and deleted the product from its platform.

In a separate case, Amway India Enterprises Pvt Ltd, Delhi, was flagged over the use of â100%â in the name â100% Pure Coconut Oilâ. The company said it had voluntarily removed the term from packaging and promotional material and discontinued old stock from sales channels.





Revised packaging without the claim has been finalised and is being rolled out progressively from September-October 2026.

In Kerala, Juza Foods, Malappuram, was flagged over multiple claims for its baby food products, including claims relating to nutrition, immunity, growth, digestion and nutrient content, besides comparisons with other milk powders. The company acknowledged the violations and agreed to remove the misleading claims.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

It also said its selling website had been shut and rectification completed, while steps were being taken for licence-related changes and an e-commerce licence.

Amway India was also flagged separately over use of the term âEnergy Drinkâ on a caffeinated beverage. The company accepted the observation and removed the term from its product range, website and promotional material. Updated packaging is to be introduced from the production cycle beginning August 2026.

The cases highlight the kinds of claims and product descriptions that can come under FSSAI scrutiny, particularly when they could influence how consumers perceive a food product.

World.title: H1N1 rising, but no cause for panic: ICMR DG
World.content:
NEW DELHI: H1N1 infections are rising across the country, but there is no cause for panic as the virus circulating is the familiar H1N1 pdm09 strain that has become a seasonal influenza virus, Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) Director General Dr Rajiv Bahl said on Tuesday.

H1N1 accounts for nearly 98% of Influenza A cases currently detected in India, while H3N2 accounts for only 2-3%, Bahl said. He stressed that the rise was consistent with the seasonal pattern of influenza and did not indicate a new or more dangerous strain.

âInfluenza is seasonal. It will keep coming every year,â Bahl said, stressing that the key concern should be a rise in severe cases, hospitalisations or deaths, rather than an increase in infections alone.

He said it was too early to say whether the current rise had peaked. Viral infections typically rise, reach a peak, remain at a plateau and then decline, but the timing can vary by a few weeks.

The surveillance network is testing samples from 73 sentinel hospitals for multiple respiratory viruses. The system includes testing for Influenza A and B, SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), human metapneumovirus and other respiratory pathogens.





A wider network of 167 virus research and diagnostic laboratories also undertakes diagnostic testing.

Bahl said there was no need to test everyone for influenza. Testing is mainly required for patients with severe disease, for whom the result can help guide treatment.

Most influenza infections are self-limiting. While most healthy people recover with supportive care, older adults, young children, pregnant women and immunocompromised people face a higher risk of complications such as pneumonia.

Antiviral medicines may be prescribed for severe or high-risk cases, while antibiotics have no role in treating viral influenza, he said.

On vaccination, Bahl said there was no urgent need for the general population to take the seasonal flu vaccine. People aged above 65 and those who are immunocompromised could discuss vaccination with their doctors. Influenza vaccination is not currently part of India's universal immunisation programme.

He also said COVID-19 and influenza are circulating together, which is not unusual. Surveillance is continuing to track any change in the pattern or severity of disease.

Basic precautions such as hand hygiene, covering the face while coughing or sneezing and staying home when unwell should be followed. Routine mask use is not considered necessary for everyone, Bahl said.

The ICMR chief said the present rise in H1N1 infections did not constitute a public health emergency.

World.title: NSA Ajit Doval holds 25th India-China border talks with Wang Yi
World.content:
Indiaâs National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi on Tuesday held the 25th round of special representativesâ talks on the India China boundary question in Beijing, with the discussions focused on maintaining peace and tranquillity along the border and advancing bilateral ties.

Earlier in the day, Doval met Chinese vice president Han Zheng ahead of the boundary talks. According to the Indian Embassy in China, the two discussed ways to strengthen peace and tranquillity in the border areas and further improve

across economic, political and multilateral forums, in line with the consensus reached by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Chinese Ambassador to India Xu Feihong said Han highlighted the momentum in bilateral ties, noting that Modi and Xi had met twice over the past two years in Kazan and Tianjin and reached a series of important understandings.

According to Xu, Han said these understandings had helped bring bilateral relations back towards recovery and improvement.

Han also called for India and China to manage their relationship from a strategic and long term perspective, strengthen mutual trust, expand cooperation, improve multilateral coordination and properly manage differences. He stressed the need for sustained and stable development of bilateral relations.





Doval arrived in Beijing on Monday for a two day visit at the invitation of Wang Yi. His visit comes amid a gradual thaw in India China relations following a series of high level engagements between Modi and Xi.

The two leaders had met on the sidelines of key international summits, including the SCO Summit in Tianjin, following their October 2024 meeting in Kazan. They had stressed that India and China are development partners rather than rivals and that differences between the two countries should not be allowed to become disputes.

During the meeting on "crime against children", Congress MP Ajay Maken submitted a letter seeking a discussion on the alleged use of pellet guns and lathicharge against students during the Jantar Mantar protest

NEW DELHI: Opposition MPs on Tuesday clashed with ruling party members during a meeting of the parliamentary standing committee on home affairs over a demand to discuss alleged police excesses against students during the July 20 protest march, news agency ANI reported, citing sources.During the meeting on "crime against children", Congress MP Ajay Maken submitted a letter seeking a discussion on the alleged use of pellet guns and lathicharge against students during the Jantar Mantar protest, sources told ANI.Congress leader Priyanka Gandhi Vadra is also learnt to have raised the issue, sources added.Opposition MPs argued that several students injured in the lathicharge were minors and that the matter therefore fell within the broader scope of 'Crime Against Children'.However, committee chairman Radha Mohan Das Agarwal rejected the demand, citing the Supreme Court's decision to set up a high-level committee to examine allegations of police excesses as well as violence by protesters during the demonstrations.Sources told ANI that a heated exchange took place between a BJP and a Congress member during the meeting, leading the chairman to ask members to restrict the discussion to the listed agenda.This comes days after the Supreme Court constituted a five-member high-powered expert committee to conduct a fact-finding exercise into allegations of police excesses during the march.The committee comprises former Punjab and Haryana high court chief justice Ravi Shankar Jha, former Delhi high court Justice Shalinder Kaur, former CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla and former Meghalaya DGP LR Bishnoi.A bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said the panel would examine grievances raised by both protesters and police authorities in connection with the demonstrations.The bench directed the HPEC to prioritise allegations of excessive use of force by police, violence by protesters, and alleged harassment and molestation of women protesters. It also allowed the panel to examine whether interim compensation should be provided to people injured during the protests, including police personnel and protesters.The Supreme Court further directed that CCTV recordings of the protests and body-camera footage from police and security personnel, which had earlier been ordered to be preserved, be handed over to the committee for examination.The court clarified that the formation of the HPEC would not prevent police or other security authorities from initiating departmental or disciplinary proceedings against officers found to have violated applicable rules.

World.title: 'Shameful': UP Congress to boycott TV debates with Ayodhya priest after spokesperson abused
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh Congress unit on Tuesday announced that none of its spokespersons will participate in TV debates with Ayodhya's Hanuman Garhi Temple priest Raju Das, accusing him of abusing and threatening party spokesperson Kunwar Singh Nishad during a live debate.

UP Congress media department chairman and former minister CP Rai said Das crossed "all limits of decency" during a debate on Doordarshan News on Monday.

In a statement, the party alleged that Das used obscene and abusive language against Nishad, including abusing his mother and issuing threats.

"The two women anchors of DD News who were part of the debate were also stunned, and the debate had to be stopped midway," Rai said, describing the incident as "shameful and unforgivable".

The Congress also demanded an impartial examination of the original recording, video footage and digital evidence of the programme. It said strict action should be taken according to law if the allegations are found to be true.

The Congress said political differences should be addressed through arguments and not personal abuse or threats.

World.title: Plea in HC to demolish and reconstruct dilapidated hostels
World.content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Tuesday directed the District Welfare Officers of the Social Justice Department to inspect hostels in southern and central districts within its jurisdiction and file a report.

A Division Bench of Justices C.V. Karthikeyan and R. Sakthivel directed the officers to inspect the hostels to ascertain building stability, the availability of basic amenities such as drinking water, electricity, cleanliness, compound wall and submit a report to the respective District Collectors in three weeks, and the Collectors should file a report to the court in two weeks thereafter.

The court was hearing a public interest litigation petition filed by K. Muruganandam of Pudukkottai district. The petitioner complained that several hostels were in dilapidated conditions posing a serious threat to students.

He said there were vacancies in various posts. Some hostels had been closed while others were operating out of rented buildings. It was the duty of the State to take necessary steps to create awareness and ensure the hostels were reopened for the benefit of students.

He sought a direction to the authorities to demolish and reconstruct hostels that were in dilapidated condition, reopen closed hostels, fill vacancies, appoint permanent full-time wardens in hostels and construct permanent buildings for hostels currently operating on rented premises. The court adjourned the hearing to November 10.

World.title: Canals desilted before water release from Mordhana Dam in Vellore, says WRD
World.content:
The Water Resources Department (WRD) has said that the left and right main canals of Mordhana Dam have been desilted before the release of water from the facility for nine days, up to September 1, for irrigation.

The reaction of WRD officials came after Vellore MP D.M. Kathir Anand claimed, in a press release, that the canals and feeder channels were not desilted completely before the scheduled release of water from the dam. The release of water, he claimed, could affect water flow especially in tail end areas for irrigation.

“A 20-member team completed periodical maintenance of the dam before water was released for irrigation. Based on requests from farmers, water has been released to fill tanks downstream,” S. Kalipriyan, Assistant Engineer (AE), WRD (Gudiyatham), told The Hindu.

Along with WRD officials, Collector P.S. Leena Alex released water from the dam to help recharge ground water in areas at least 10 km downstream. Every day, on an average, 225 cusecs of water from the left and right canals of the dam will be released. In other words, 174.96 mcft of water will be released during this period. “Water from the dam will help cultivate paddy, groundnuts, and banana along the river as most of the water bodies have become dry. Most farmers in the region depend on borewells for irrigation,” said T. Pasupathi, a farmer.

At present, the dam has 235.03 mcft of water as against its total storage capacity of 261.3 mcft of water. The water from the reservoir, which is built across the Koundinya River, a tributary of the Palar, will benefit nine tanks in Gudiyatham and Katpadi taluks.

These tanks enable farming activities on around 2,500 acres and also help recharge ground water in their vicinity. While water from the Koundinya River directly irrigates around 140 acres, another 220 acres are irrigated through water from the canals. The left canal supports irrigation activities in the ayacut areas attached to seven tanks.

WRD officials said that the left canal was restored in July 2025 under the Rehabilitation and Restoration of Lakes scheme 2024-25. Deposited silt on the canal bed was removed to a depth of three metres to ensure steady water flow. Growth of thick vegetation, especially on the bund and its slope was also removed, officials said.

The left canal runs for a distance of 31.84 km, covering 19 villages with 1,710.92 hectares of farmland. With a width of three metres, it covers a large tract of land under cultivation that resulted in silt deposition over the years.

World.title: Farmer electrocuted in Ranipet
World.content:
A 58-year-old farmer was electrocuted as he switched on a motor pump set in his farmland at Pulivalam village near Sholinghur town in Ranipet.

The deceased was identified as P. Babu. Initial inquiry revealed that it was around 7 a.m. when Babu went to his farmland to irrigate paddy fields and switched on the motor pump set. He was electrocuted. The region was also witnessing rains for the past few days.

Immediately, his neighbours disconnected the power supply. They also informed Kondapalayam police who reached the spot and registered a case. The police said that an electrical short circuit could have resulted in the incident. A probe is under way.
